declarations.docstring:
Does the set of integers of the form $n + \varphi(n)$ have positive (lower) density?

[GIL24] proved this was true.
references: [erdosproblems.com/822](https://www.erdosproblems.com/822)
[GIL24] Gabdullin, Mikhail R. and Iudelevich, Vitalii V. and Luca, Florian, Numbers of the form {$k+f(k)$}. J. Number Theory (2024), 58--85.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ (Set.range fun n => n + n.totient).HasPosDensity

declarations.docstring:
Is there an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that every integer $n$ with
$\sigma(n) > Cn$ is the distinct sum of proper divisors of $n$?

This has been solved in the affirmative by Larsen - in fact, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $L$
such that if $n$ has only prime divisors $>L$ and $\sigma(n)>(2+\epsilon)n$ then $n$ is the distinct
sum of proper divisors of $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/825](https://www.erdosproblems.com/825)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ C, ∃ (_ : C > 0), ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) > C * ↑n → ∃ s ⊆ n.properDivisors, n = s.sum id

declarations.docstring:
Show that if the constant $C > 0$ is such that every integer $n$ with
$\sigma(n) > Cn$ is the distinct sum of proper divisors of $n$, then we
must have $C > 2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/825](https://www.erdosproblems.com/825)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (C : ℝ),
  0 < C → (∀ (n : ℕ), ↑((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) > C * ↑n → ∃ s ⊆ n.properDivisors, n = s.sum id) → 2 < C

declarations.docstring:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k\geq 1$
$$
  \tau(n + k) \ll k?
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/826](https://www.erdosproblems.com/826)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ C > 0, {n | ∀ k ≥ 1, ↑((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) (n + k)) ≤ C * ↑k}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (a : ℤ), {n | ↑n.totient ∣ ↑n + a}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: When $n > 1$, Lehmer conjectured that $\phi(n) | n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.
references: [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ n > 1, n.totient ∣ n - 1 ↔ Prime n

declarations.docstring:
It is an easy exercise to show that $\phi(n) | n$ if and only if $n = 0, 1$ or $n = 2^a 3^b$ for
some $a > 0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, n.totient ∣ n ↔ n ≤ 1 ∨ ∃ a > 0, ∃ b, n = 2 ^ a * 3 ^ b

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 829 (open).**  Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be the set of perfect cubes.  Is
it true that $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \ll (\log n)^{O(1)}$?  That is, does there exist a natural
number $C$ such that the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is
$O((\log n)^C)$ as $n \to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ C, (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log ↑n ^ C

declarations.docstring:
Membership in `cubes` can be witnessed by a bounded cube root, which makes it
decidable for concrete values.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (m : ℕ), m ∈ Erdos829.cubes ↔ ∃ k < m + 1, k ^ 3 = m

declarations.docstring:
The Hardy-Ramanujan taxicab number satisfies $1729 = 1^3 + 12^3 = 9^3 + 10^3$, giving
the four ordered representations $(1, 1728), (1728, 1), (729, 1000), (1000, 729)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 1729 = 4

declarations.docstring: The integer $3$ is not the sum of two cubes.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 3 = 0

declarations.docstring: The only ordered pair of cubes summing to $2$ is $(1, 1)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 2 = 1

declarations.docstring: There is exactly one ordered pair of cubes summing to $0$, namely $(0, 0)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 0 = 1

declarations.docstring:
Mahler proved $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \gg (\log n)^{1/4}$ for infinitely many $n$, where $A$ is
the set of perfect cubes.

[Ma35b] Mahler, K., _On the lattice points on curves of genus 1_. Proc. London Math. Soc.
  (2) (1935), 431-466.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C > 0, ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, C * Real.log ↑n ^ (1 / 4) ≤ ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes n)

declarations.docstring:
Mordell proved $\limsup_{n \to \infty} (1_A \ast 1_A)(n) = \infty$, where $A$ is the set of
perfect cubes.  Equivalently, the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is
unbounded.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤

Stewart improved Mahler's lower bound to $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \gg (\log n)^{11/13}$ for

declarations.docstring:
**Erdos Problem 830, Part 1**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$. Are there
infinitely many amicable pairs?

**Erdos Problem 830, Part 2**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then is it true that
$$A(x) > x^{1-o(1)}?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)

declarations.docstring:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that $A(x) = o(x)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)

declarations.docstring:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\log x)^{1/3})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)

declarations.docstring:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))(\log x\log\log x)^{1/2})$.

declarations.docstring:
It is known that for $3 \leq k \leq 8$, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is greater than
$k+1$, see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {k : ℕ}, 3 ≤ k → k ≤ 8 → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring:
It is also known that for $3 \leq k \leq 203$ odd, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is
greater than $k+1$, see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {k : ℕ}, 3 ≤ k → k ≤ 300 → Odd k → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring: Johnson's bound for the chromatic number of the Johnson graph.
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, ↑⌈↑(n.choose k) / ↑(Erdos835.johnsonBound n 4 k)⌉₊ ≤ (SimpleGraph.johnson n k).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist a $k>2$ such that the $k$-sized subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with
$k+1$ colours such that for every $A\subset \{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k+1$ all $k+1$
colours appear among the $k$-sized subsets of $A$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: (∃ k > 2, Erdos835.Property k) ↔ True

declarations.docstring:
Alternative statement of Erdős Problem 835 using the chromatic number of the Johnson graph.
This is equivalent to asking whether there exists $k > 2$ such that the chromatic number of the
Johnson graph $J(2k, k)$ is $k+1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: (∃ l, (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * (l + 3)) (l + 3)).chromaticNumber = ↑(l + 3) + 1) ↔ True

declarations.docstring: Johnson's bound for the independence number of the Johnson graph.
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, (SimpleGraph.johnson n k).indepNum ≤ Erdos835.johnsonBound n 4 k

declarations.docstring:
The smallest case not on this page is $k=9$:
But that one can be solved as well:
The chromatic number of $J(18, 9)$ is at least $11$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: (SimpleGraph.johnson 18 9).chromaticNumber > 9 + 1

declarations.docstring:
It is known that for $3 \leq k \leq 8$, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is greater than $k+1$,
see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → k ≤ 8 → (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber > ↑k + 1

declarations.docstring: Ma and Tang's result implies the cases for odd $k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
(∀ (k : ℕ), 2 < k → (k + 1).Composite → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber) →
  ∀ (k : ℕ), 2 < k → Odd k → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring: Is the chromatic number of `J(2 * k, k)` always at least `k + 2`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)

declarations.docstring:
Ma and Tang have proved that the chromatic number of $J(2k,k)$ is $>k+1$ for all $k>2$ not of the
form $p-1$ for prime $p$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 2 < k → (k + 1).Composite → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring: It can be seen that the chromatic number of $J(2k,k)$ is $>k+1$ for all odd $k>2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 2 < k → Odd k → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber

references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)

declarations.docstring:
Let $C > 0$. Is it true that the set of integers of the form $n = b_1 + \cdots + b_t$,
with $b_1 < \cdots < b_t$, where $b_i = 2^{k_i}3^{l_i}$ for $1 \leq i\leq t$ and
$b_t \leq Cb_1$ has density $0$?

van Doorn and Everts \cite{vDEv25} have disproved this with $C=6$ - in fact, they prove that all
integers can be written as such a sum in which $b_t<6b_1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/845](https://www.erdosproblems.com/845)
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (C : ℝ),
    0 < C →
      have f := fun x =>
        match x with
        | (k, l) => 2 ^ k * 3 ^ l;
      {x | ∃ B, ∃ (h : B.Nonempty) (_ : ↑(B.sup f) ≤ C * ↑(B.inf' h f)), ∑ x ∈ B, f x = x}.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 846**
Let `A ⊂ ℝ²` be an infinite set for which there exists some `ϵ>0` such that in any subset of `A`
of size `n` there are always at least `ϵn` with no three on a line.
Is it true that `A` is the union of a finite number of sets where no three are on a line?

In other words, prove or disprove the following statement: every infinite `ε`-non-trilinear subset of the
plane is weakly non-trilinar.
references: [erdosproblems.com/846](https://www.erdosproblems.com/846)
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
    ∀ ε > 0, A.Infinite → Erdos846.NonTrilinearFor A ε → Erdos846.WeaklyNonTrilinear A

declarations.docstring:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set for which there exists some $\epsilon > 0$ such that
in any subset of $A$ of size $n$ there is a subset of size at least $\epsilon n$ which contains no
three-term arithmetic progression.

Is it true that $A$ is the union of a finite number of sets which contain no three-term arithmetic
progression?

A negative answer was given by Reiher, Rödl, and Sales [RRS24], who proved that, for any
$0<\mu<1/2$, there exists $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that every finite colouring of $A$ contains
a three-term arithmetic progression, and yet every subset of $A$ of size $n$ contains a subset of
size $\geq \mu n$ without a three-term arithmetic progression.
references: [erdosproblems.com/847](https://www.erdosproblems.com/847)

[RRS24] Reiher, Christian and R\"odl, Vojt\v ech and Sales, Marcelo, Colouring versus density in integers and {H}ales-{J}ewett cubes. J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) (2024) [arXiv:2311.08556](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.08556)
declarations.type_pretty: False ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Infinite ↑A → Erdos847.HasFew3APs A → ∃ n S, (∀ (i : Fin n), ThreeAPFree (S i)) ∧ A = ⋃ i, S i

declarations.docstring:
Is the maximum size of a set $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never squarefree
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/848](https://www.erdosproblems.com/848)
[Er92b] Erdős, P. "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry." Resenhas do Instituto de Matemático e Estatística da Universidade de São Paulo 2.2 (1995): 165-186.
[Sa25] Sawhney, M. "Problem 848." (2025) https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf
Full formal proof of asymptotic result: https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (N : ℕ), Erdos848.Erdos848For N

declarations.docstring:
There exists $N₀$ such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfies that $ab + 1$
is never squarefree for all $a, b ∈ A$, then $|A| ≤ |\{n ≤ N : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}|$.

More precisely, Sawhney proves: there exist absolute constants $η > 0$ and $N₀$
such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $|A| ≥ (1/25 - η)N$ then $A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}$ or
$A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 18 \pmod{25}\}$.

A complete formal Lean 4 proof is available at:
https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
references: [erdosproblems.com/848](https://www.erdosproblems.com/848)
[Er92b] Erdős, P. "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry." Resenhas do Instituto de Matemático e Estatística da Universidade de São Paulo 2.2 (1995): 165-186.
[Sa25] Sawhney, M. "Problem 848." (2025) https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf
Full formal proof of asymptotic result: https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos848.Erdos848For N

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every integer $t\geq1$, there is some integer $a$ such that ${n \choose k} = a$
with $1\leq k \le \frac{n}{2}$ has exactly $t$ solutions?
references: [erdosproblems.com/849](https://www.erdosproblems.com/849)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ t ≥ 1, ∃ a, {n | ∃ k ≥ 1, 2 * k ≤ n ∧ n.choose k = a}.ncard = t

declarations.docstring: Is it true that, for all large $n$, $f(n + 1) \ge f(n)$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/85](https://www.erdosproblems.com/85)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos85.f n ≤ Erdos85.f (n + 1)

declarations.docstring:
Can there exist two distinct integers $x$ and $y$ such that $x,y$ have the same prime factors,
$x+1,y+1$ have the same prime factors, and $x+2,y+2$ also have the same prime factors?
references: [erdosproblems.com/850](https://www.erdosproblems.com/850)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ x y,
    x ≠ y ∧
      x.primeFactors = y.primeFactors ∧
        (x + 1).primeFactors = (y + 1).primeFactors ∧ (x + 2).primeFactors = (y + 2).primeFactors

declarations.docstring:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some $r \ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the
form $2^k+n$, where $k \geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

This was proved affirmatively by Price and GPT-5.2 Pro [Pr26].
references: [erdosproblems.com/851](https://www.erdosproblems.com/851)
[Pr26] D. Price and GPT-5.2 Pro, [Erdős problem 851](https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1, ∃ r d, (Erdos851.TwoPowAddSet r).HasDensity d ∧ 1 - ε ≤ d

declarations.docstring:
The set of integers of the form `2^k+p` (where `p` is prime) has positive lower density.

Formalisation note: here we also allow `p = 1` since this simplifies the code and is equivalent
to the original statement.
references: [erdosproblems.com/851](https://www.erdosproblems.com/851)
[Pr26] D. Price and GPT-5.2 Pro, [Erdős problem 851](https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty: 0 < (Erdos851.TwoPowAddSet 1).lowerDensity

declarations.docstring:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) \to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/853](https://www.erdosproblems.com/853)
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto Erdos853.r Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $r(x)$ be the smallest even
integer $t$ such that $d_n = t$ has no solutions for $n \le x$.

Is it true that $r(x) / \log x \to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/853](https://www.erdosproblems.com/853)
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos853.r n) / Real.log ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for sufficiently large $x, y$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) (y : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (x + y).primeCounting ≤ x.primeCounting + y.primeCounting

declarations.docstring: Estimate `m(n,k)`, or better give an asymptotic formula.
references: [erdosproblems.com/857](https://www.erdosproblems.com/857)
declarations.type_pretty:
have f := sorry;
∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos857.m n k) / f k n) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

declarations.docstring: The density of the divisor sum set is asymptotically equivalent to $c_1 / \log(t)^{c_2}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/859](https://www.erdosproblems.com/859)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c₁ > 0,
  ∃ c₂ > 0,
    ∃ d,
      (∀ t > 0, (Erdos859.DivisorSumSet t).HasDensity (d t)) ∧
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun t => d t) fun t => c₁ / Real.log ↑t ^ c₂

declarations.docstring:
A weaker version of the problem proved by Erdos:
The density `dₜ` of `DivisorSumSet (t : ℕ)` is bounded from below by `1 / log (t) ^ c₃` and
from above by `1 / log (t) ^ c₄` for some positive constants `c₃` and `c₄`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/859](https://www.erdosproblems.com/859)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c₃ > 0,
  ∃ c₄ > 0,
    ∃ t₀,
      ∀ᶠ (t : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∃ dₜ, (Erdos859.DivisorSumSet t).HasDensity dₜ ∧ 1 / Real.log ↑t ^ c₃ < dₜ ∧ dₜ < 1 / Real.log ↑t ^ c₄

declarations.docstring:
An easy sanity check is to prove that for every natural number `t` the density `dₜ` is
a positive number.
Hint: investigate some multiplicative structure of `DivisorSumSet t`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/859](https://www.erdosproblems.com/859)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (t : ℕ), (Erdos859.DivisorSumSet t).HasPosDensity

declarations.docstring: A case where we can easily calculate the density of `DivisorSumSet t` is that of `t=0`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/859](https://www.erdosproblems.com/859)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos859.DivisorSumSet 0 = Set.univ

declarations.docstring:
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for all large $N$, if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
size at least $\frac{5}{8}N+C$ then there are distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that $a+b,a+c,b+c\in A$.

A problem of Erdős and Sós (also earlier considered by Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75], but Erdős
had forgotten this).
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      ↑A.card ≥ 5 / 8 * ↑N + C → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a + b ∈ A ∧ a + c ∈ A ∧ b + c ∈ A

declarations.docstring:
It is a classical folklore fact that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,2N\}$ has size $\geq N+2$ then
there are distinct $a,b\in A$ such that $a+b\in A$, which establishes the $k=2$ case.
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (N : ℕ), ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 (2 * N), A.card ≥ N + 2 → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ a + b ∈ A

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Sós conjectured that
$f_k(N)\sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1+\sum_{1\leq r\leq k-2}\frac{1}{4^r}\right) N$,
where $f_k(N)$ is the minimal size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ guaranteeing $k$ elements
have all pairwise sums in the set.
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  2 ≤ k →
    Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun N => ↑(Erdos865.f N k)) fun N =>
      1 / 2 * (1 + ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (k - 2), (1 / 4) ^ r) * ↑N

declarations.docstring:
Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75] have proved that, for all $k\geq 3$, there exists $\epsilon_k>0$
such that (for large enough $N$) $f_k(N)\leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\epsilon_k\right)N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ∃ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos865.f N k) ≤ (2 / 3 - ε) * ↑N

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then
must $A$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] answered this in the negative.
references: [erdosproblems.com/868](https://www.erdosproblems.com/868)
[LaLa26] Larsen and Larsen, [Erdős problem 868](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/blob/main/868.pdf) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => Erdos868.ncard_add_repr A 2 n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
        ∃ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) > \epsilon \log n$ for large $n$
and an arbitrary fixed $\epsilon > 0$, then must $A$ contain a minimal additive
basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] constructed a counterexample with $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/868](https://www.erdosproblems.com/868)
[LaLa26] Larsen and Larsen, [Erdős problem 868](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/blob/main/868.pdf) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    ∀ ε > 0,
      A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ε * Real.log ↑n < ↑(Erdos868.ncard_add_repr A 2 n)) →
          ∃ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

declarations.docstring:
Härtter and Nathanson proved that there exist additive bases which do not contain
any minimal additive bases.
references: [erdosproblems.com/868](https://www.erdosproblems.com/868)
[LaLa26] Larsen and Larsen, [Erdős problem 868](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/blob/main/868.pdf) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (o : ℕ),
  1 < o →
    ∃ A,
      A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o ∧
        ∀ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o → ∃ b ∈ B, (B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Nathanson proved that this is true if $f(n) > (\log \frac{4}{3})^{-1} \log n$ for
all large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/868](https://www.erdosproblems.com/868)
[LaLa26] Larsen and Larsen, [Erdős problem 868](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/blob/main/868.pdf) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (Real.log (4 / 3))⁻¹ * Real.log ↑n < ↑(Erdos868.ncard_add_repr A 2 n)) →
        ∃ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, and suppose $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Can $A$ be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases of order $2$?

A question of Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa88], who proved this is true if $1_A\ast 1_A(n) > c\log n$ (for all large $n$) for some constant $c>(\log\frac{4}{3})^{-1}$. Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa89] also proved that for every $t$ there exists a basis $A$ of order $2$ such that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\geq t$ for all large $n$ and yet $A$ cannot be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases. This has been disproved by Larsen using Claude Opus 4.5 - in fact only a small modification of the argument of [ErNa89] is required.
references: [erdosproblems.com/871](https://www.erdosproblems.com/871)
[ErNa88] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Partitions of bases into disjoint unions of bases*. J. Number Theory (1988), 1-9.
[ErNa89] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Additive bases with many representations*. Acta Arith. (1989), 399-406.
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    ((∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, a + b = n) ∧
        ∀ (t : ℕ),
          ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
            ∃ pairs, pairs.card ≥ t ∧ ∀ p ∈ pairs, p.1 ∈ A ∧ p.2 ∈ A ∧ p.1 + p.2 = n ∧ p.1 ≤ p.2) →
      ∃ B C,
        (∀ (x : ℕ), x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ B ∨ x ∈ C) ∧
          Disjoint B C ∧
            (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ B, ∃ b ∈ B, a + b = n) ∧
              ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ C, ∃ b ∈ C, a + b = n

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 872, part (i) (weak form): there exists a constant $\epsilon > 0$ such that the
game length is at least $\epsilon \cdot n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
[erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos872.L n) ≥ ε * ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 872, part (ii) (strong form): for every $\epsilon > 0$, the game length is at
least $(1-\epsilon) \cdot n / 2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

Status note: the forum thread (April-May 2026) records Shortener strategies giving
$L(n) \leq (23/48 + o(1)) \cdot n$ (described in the thread as accepted as correct, with a Lean
formalization in progress) and a claimed $L(n) \leq 0.19 \cdot n$, either of which would answer this
question negatively under the Prolonger-first convention. Neither is published, so the statement
is recorded here as the original Erdős question.
references: [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
[erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos872.L n) ≥ (1 - ε) * ↑n / 2

declarations.docstring:
A trivial upper bound: a play can claim at most the $n - 1$ elements of $\{2, \dots, n\}$, so
$L(n) \leq n - 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
[erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → Erdos872.L n ≤ n - 1

declarations.docstring:
Forum-related variant: how small can a maximal primitive subset of $\{2, \dots, n\}$ be?
The set of primes in $\{2, \dots, n\}$ is a maximal primitive subset of size $\pi(n)$, and the forum
thread asks whether this is the smallest possible for all $n \geq 2$. Equivalently: must every
completed play of the saturation game, by both players and regardless of strategy, claim at least
$\pi(n)$ elements? (Terminal positions of the game are exactly the maximal primitive subsets.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
[erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ n ≥ 2,
    ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), Maximal (Erdos872.IsPrimitive n) A → (Finset.filter Nat.Prime (Finset.Icc 2 n)).card ≤ A.card

declarations.docstring:
Each move claims exactly one pool element, so the minimax value never exceeds the number of
already claimed elements plus the number of still unclaimed elements.
references: [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
[erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {n : ℕ} (fuel : ℕ) (turn : Bool) (p : Erdos872.GamePos n),
  Erdos872.gameValueAux fuel turn p ≤ p.claimed.card + p.pool.card

declarations.docstring:
Membership in `legalMoves`: a legal move is a pool element whose insertion preserves
primitiveness.
references: [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
[erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {n : ℕ} {p : Erdos872.GamePos n} {x : ℕ},
  x ∈ Erdos872.legalMoves p ↔ x ∈ p.pool ∧ Erdos872.IsPrimitive n (insert x p.claimed)

declarations.docstring:
Let $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and let $F(A,X,k)$ count the number of $i$
such that $[a_i,a_{i+1}, \dots ,a_{i+k−1}] < X$, where the left-hand side is the least common
multiple. Is it true that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists some $k$ such that
$F(A,X,k) < X^\epsilon$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/873](https://www.erdosproblems.com/873)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ ε > 0, 0 < a 0 → StrictMono a → ∃ k, ∀ X > 0, ↑↑(Erdos873.F a X k) < ↑(X ^ ε)

declarations.docstring:
Let `A ⊂ ℕ` be an additive basis of order `k` which is minimal in the sense that
if `B ⊂ A` is any infinite set, then `A \ B` is not a basis of order `k`.

Must there exist an infinite `B ⊂ A` such that `A \ B`
is an additive basis of order `k + 1`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/881](https://www.erdosproblems.com/881)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ),
    Erdos881.IsMinimalAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder k A → ∃ B ⊆ A, B.Infinite ∧ (A \ B).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder (k + 1)

declarations.docstring:
For a natural number n, let $1 = d_1 < \dotsc < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ denote the divisors of $n$
in increasing order.
Does it hold that
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \ll 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$
for $n \to \infty`, i.e.
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \in O \left( 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}) \right)$?

This conjecture has been **disproved**:
- In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer assuming the prime tuples
  conjecture, see `erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` for this implication.
- Daniel Larsen subsequently gave an
  [unconditional disproof](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf).

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
references: [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
[Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf)
[Larsen](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: False ↔ Erdos884.Erdos884Prop

declarations.docstring:
In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer to Erdos conjecture 884,
disproving it under the assumption of the *Qualitative Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture*.
See [here](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf).
The *qualitative* version of the conjecture only states that there are infinitely many tuples
of primes and does not require any asymptotical bounds and as such is a corollary of the general
form of the Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture.
We state the 'weaker' implication using general Hardy-Littlewood here, since this conjecture is
already formalized.
references: [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
[Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf)
[Larsen](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ) (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m → ¬Erdos884.Erdos884Prop

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every $k \geq 1$, there exist integers $N_1 < \dots < N_k$ such that
$|\cap_i D(N_i)| \geq k$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/885](https://www.erdosproblems.com/885)
[ErRo97] Erdős, P. and Rosenfeld, M., The factor-difference set of integers. (1997)
[Ji99] Jiménez-Urroz, J., A note on a conjecture of Erdős and {R}osenfeld. (1999)
[Br19] Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdős related to common factor differences. (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∃ Ns, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = k ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, Erdos885.factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ k

declarations.docstring: Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved this is true for $k=2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/885](https://www.erdosproblems.com/885)
[ErRo97] Erdős, P. and Rosenfeld, M., The factor-difference set of integers. (1997)
[Ji99] Jiménez-Urroz, J., A note on a conjecture of Erdős and {R}osenfeld. (1999)
[Br19] Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdős related to common factor differences. (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ Ns, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = 2 ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, Erdos885.factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 2

declarations.docstring: Jiménez-Urroz [Ji99] proved this for $k=3$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/885](https://www.erdosproblems.com/885)
[ErRo97] Erdős, P. and Rosenfeld, M., The factor-difference set of integers. (1997)
[Ji99] Jiménez-Urroz, J., A note on a conjecture of Erdős and {R}osenfeld. (1999)
[Br19] Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdős related to common factor differences. (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ Ns, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = 3 ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, Erdos885.factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 3

declarations.docstring: Bremner [Br19] proved this for $k=4$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/885](https://www.erdosproblems.com/885)
[ErRo97] Erdős, P. and Rosenfeld, M., The factor-difference set of integers. (1997)
[Ji99] Jiménez-Urroz, J., A note on a conjecture of Erdős and {R}osenfeld. (1999)
[Br19] Bremner, A., On a problem of Erdős related to common factor differences. (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ Ns, (∀ n ∈ Ns, 1 ≤ n) ∧ Ns.card = 4 ∧ (⋂ n ∈ Ns, Erdos885.factorDifferenceSet n).ncard ≥ 4

declarations.docstring:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Is it true that, for all large $n$, the number of divisors of $n$ in
$(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+n^{1/2-\epsilon})$ is $O_\epsilon(1)$?

Erdős attributes this conjecture to Ruzsa.
references: [erdosproblems.com/886](https://www.erdosproblems.com/886)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ K, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (Erdos886.Erdos886Divisors n ε 1).card ≤ K

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved that, for any constant $C>0$, all large $n$ have at most
$1+C^2$ many divisors in $[n^{1/2}, n^{1/2}+Cn^{1/4}]$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/886](https://www.erdosproblems.com/886)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ C > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ↑{d ∈ n.divisors | ↑n ^ (1 / 2) ≤ ↑d ∧ ↑d ≤ ↑n ^ (1 / 2) + C * ↑n ^ (1 / 4)}.card ≤ 1 + C ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Rosenfeld [ErRo97] proved that there are infinitely many $n$ such that there are
four divisors of $n$ in $(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+16n^{1/4})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/886](https://www.erdosproblems.com/886)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty: {n | 4 ≤ (Erdos886.Erdos886Divisors n (1 / 4) 16).card}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/887](https://www.erdosproblems.com/887)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ C > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, {d ∈ Finset.Ioo ⌊√↑n⌋₊ ⌈√↑n + C * ↑n ^ (1 / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n}.card ≤ sorry

declarations.docstring:
Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/887](https://www.erdosproblems.com/887)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ K, ∀ C > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, {d ∈ Finset.Ioo ⌊√↑n⌋₊ ⌈√↑n + C * ↑n ^ (1 / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n}.card ≤ K

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Rosenfeld, ask whether $4$ is the best possible $K$ for the infinitude of $n$
with (at least) $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/887](https://www.erdosproblems.com/887)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty: IsGreatest {K | ∃ C > 0, Infinite ↑{n | K ≤ {d ∈ Finset.Ioo ⌊√↑n⌋₊ ⌈√↑n + C * ↑n ^ (1 / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n}.card}} 4

declarations.docstring:
A question of Erdős and Rosenfeld, who proved that there are infinitely many $n$ with (at least)
$4$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + cn^{\frac{1}{4}})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/887](https://www.erdosproblems.com/887)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C > 0, Infinite ↑{n | 4 ≤ {d ∈ Finset.Ioo ⌊√↑n⌋₊ ⌈√↑n + C * ↑n ^ (1 / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n}.card}

declarations.docstring:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that if
$a\leq b\leq c\leq d\in A$ are such that $abcd$ is a square then $ad=bc$?

This was proved by GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted by Chojecki).
references: [erdosproblems.com/888](https://www.erdosproblems.com/888)
[Er98] Erdős, Paul, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Nat.findGreatest (Erdos888.p n) n)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n * Real.log (Real.log ↑n) / Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring: The primes show that $\lvert A\rvert \gg n/\log n$ is possible.
references: [erdosproblems.com/888](https://www.erdosproblems.com/888)
[Er98] Erdős, Paul, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑n / Real.log ↑n) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Nat.findGreatest (Erdos888.p n) n)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős claims that Sárközy proved that $\lvert A\rvert =o(n)$ (a proof of this
bound is provided by Tao in the comments).
references: [erdosproblems.com/888](https://www.erdosproblems.com/888)
[Er98] Erdős, Paul, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Nat.findGreatest (Erdos888.p n) n)) =o[Filter.atTop] Nat.cast

declarations.docstring:
Cambie and Weisenberg have noted in the comments that the set of semiprimes
also works, showing $(1+o(1))\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n \leq \lvert A\rvert$ is achievable.
references: [erdosproblems.com/888](https://www.erdosproblems.com/888)
[Er98] Erdős, Paul, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑n * Real.log (Real.log ↑n) / Real.log ↑n) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Nat.findGreatest (Erdos888.p n) n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $v(n,k)$ count the prime factors of $n+k$ which
do not divide $n+i$ for $0\leq i < k$. Is it true that
$v_0(n)=\max_{k\geq 0}v(n,k)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/889](https://www.erdosproblems.com/889)
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto Erdos889.v₀ Filter.atTop (nhds ⊤)

declarations.docstring:
Does $V_1(n) = 1$ have finite solutions?

This is a modification of `erdos_889.variants.v1_eq_1_finite`,
which might make it more amenable to attack according to [ErSe67].

[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
references: [erdosproblems.com/889](https://www.erdosproblems.com/889)
declarations.type_pretty: sorry ↔ {n | Erdos889.V_l 1 n = 1}.Finite

declarations.docstring:
Let $v_l(n) = \max_{k\geq l} v(n,k)$. For every fixed $l$,

declarations.docstring:
If $\omega_k(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ which are $>k$, then is it true
that, for every $k\geq 1$,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega_k(n+i)\leq k?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?
references: [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 1,
    Filter.limsup
        (fun n =>
          (∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n + i))) *
            (↑(Real.log (Real.log ↑n)) / ↑(Real.log ↑n)))
        Filter.atTop =
      1

declarations.docstring:
A question of Erdős and Selfridge [ErSe67], who observe that
$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\geq k+\pi(k)-1$ for every $k$. This follows from
Pólya's theorem that the set of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded gaps - indeed,
$n(n+1)\cdots (n+k-1)$ is divisible by all primes $\leq k$ and, provided $n$ is large, all but at
most one of $n,n+1,\ldots,n+k-1$ has a prime factor $>k$ by Pólya's theorem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  Filter.liminf (fun n => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n + i))) Filter.atTop ≥
    ↑k + ↑k.primeCounting - 1

declarations.docstring: It is a classical fact that $\limsup_{n\to \infty}\omega(n)\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1.$
references: [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

    Filter.atTop =
  1

declarations.docstring:
Let $2=p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large
$n$, there must exist an integer in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k)$ with $>k$ many prime factors?
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Finset.Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i), k < ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m

declarations.docstring:

(sufficiently large) consecutive integers there must exist one with at least $3$ prime factors?
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture

declarations.docstring:
Schinzel deduced from Pólya's theorem [Po18] (that the sequence of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded
gaps) that this is true with $p_1\cdots p_k$ replaced by $p_1\cdots p_{k-1}p_{k+1}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ k ≥ 2,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ m ∈ Finset.Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k - 1), Nat.nth Nat.Prime i) * Nat.nth Nat.Prime k),
      k < ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m

declarations.docstring:
Weisenberg has observed that Dickson's conjecture implies the answer is no if we replace
$p_1\cdots p_k$ with $p_1\cdots p_k-1$. Indeed, let $L_k$ be the lowest common multiple of all
integers at most $p_1\cdots p_k$. By Dickson's conjecture [Wikipedia], there are infinitely many
$n'$ such that $\frac{L_k}{m}n'+1$ is prime for all $1\leq m < p_1\cdots p_k$. It follows that,
if $n=L_kn'+1$, then all integers in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k-1)$ have at most $k$ prime factors.
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture
declarations.type_pretty:
Erdos891.DicksonConjecture →
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ m ∈ Finset.Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i - 1),
        ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m ≤ k

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$ such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The answer is no; this follows from a construction of Wirsing [Wi81], rediscovered by
Archivara [Ar25] and formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
references: [erdosproblems.com/897](https://www.erdosproblems.com/897)
[Ar25] Archivara Math Research Agent, [An Additive Counterexample: Erdős Problem 897](https://archivara.org/paper/df04f023-6ef0-4c52-bd12-18cdaa8f0741) (2025)
[ArWu25] Aristotle, operated mostly by L. Wu, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 897](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean) (2025)
[Wi70] E. Wirsing, A characterization of $\log n$ as an additive arithmetic function. Symposia Math. (1970), 45-57.
[Wi81] E. Wirsing, Additive and completely additive functions with restricted growth. Recent progress in analytic number theory, Vol. 2 (Durham, 1979), 231--280 (1981).
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ a > 0, ∀ b > 0, a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
      Filter.limsup
            (fun x =>
              match x with
              | (p, k) => ↑(f (p ^ k)) / ↑(Real.log (↑p ^ k)))
            (Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) | Nat.Prime p}) =
          ⊤ →
        Filter.limsup (fun n => (↑(f (n + 1)) - ↑(f n)) / ↑(Real.log ↑n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A - A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} = \infty?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa [Ru78].

[Ru78] Ruzsa, I. Z., _On the cardinality of {$A+A$}\ and {$A-A$}_. (1978), 933--938.
references: [erdosproblems.com/899](https://www.erdosproblems.com/899)

        Filter.limsup (fun N => ↑((A - A) ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard / ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard) Filter.atTop = ⊤

$n^{1+O(\frac{1}{\log\log n})}$ many pairs which are distance $1$ apart?

This was
[disproved](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/74c24085-19b0-4534-9c90-465b8e29ad73/unit-distance-proof.pdf)
by an internal model at OpenAI, which constructed (for infinitely many $n$) a set $P$ of $n$ points
in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that the number of unit distance pairs in $P$ is at least $n^{1+c}$, where
$c > 0$ is an absolute constant.
references: [erdosproblems.com/90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90)

      (fun n => ↑(Erdos90.maxUnitDistances n)) =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ (1 + O n)

declarations.docstring:
**Constructive form of the disproof.** There is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that
infinitely many $n$ admit a configuration realising at least $n^{1+c}$ unit distances.

This is the qualitative content of Theorem 1.1 of Alon–Bloom–Gowers–Litt–Sawin–Shankar–
Tsimerman–Wang–Matchett Wood, [*Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695)
(2026). An explicit bound $c \ge 0.014114$ is given by Sawin, [*An explicit lower bound for the
unit distance problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579) (2026); see
`erdos_90.variants.sawin_explicit` below.
references: [erdosproblems.com/90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, {n | ↑n ^ (1 + c) ≤ ↑(Erdos90.maxUnitDistances n)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
The polynomial lower bound implies the answer to Erdős 90 is `False`: a fixed positive
exponent $c$ is incompatible with the conjectured $O(1 / \log \log n)$ growth.
references: [erdosproblems.com/90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90)
declarations.type_pretty:
(∃ c > 0, {n | ↑n ^ (1 + c) ≤ ↑(Erdos90.maxUnitDistances n)}.Infinite) →
  (False ↔
    ∃ O,
      ∃ (_ : O =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => 1 / Real.log (Real.log ↑n)),
        (fun n => ↑(Erdos90.maxUnitDistances n)) =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ (1 + O n))

(2026).
references: [erdosproblems.com/90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90)

declarations.docstring:
**Sawin's Lemma 2: lattice geometry of unit distances** (Sawin, [arXiv:2605.20579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579)).

Let $d \ge 1$, $R \ge 2$, and suppose $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^{2d}$ is a lattice equipped with
an additive embedding $\pi : \Lambda \to \mathbb{R}^2$. Suppose $S \subseteq \Lambda$ is a finite
set of "matching" vectors satisfying $\|v\| \le 1$ and $\|\pi v\| = 1$ for every $v \in S$. Then
there is a finite point set $U \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with unit-distance density at least
$(1 - 1/R)^{2d}\,\#S$, i.e. $(1-1/R)^{2d}\,\#S\,\#U \le \#\{\text{unit pairs in } U\}$.

This pure geometry-of-numbers reduction is the elementary heart of the disproof.
references: [erdosproblems.com/90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (d : ℕ),
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ (R : ℝ),
      2 ≤ R →
        ∀ (Λ : Submodule ℤ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (2 * d)))) (π : ↥Λ →+ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
          Function.Injective ⇑π →
            ∀ (S : Finset ↥Λ),
              (∀ v ∈ S, ‖↑v‖ ≤ 1) →
                (∀ v ∈ S, ‖π v‖ = 1) →
                  ∃ U,
                    0 < U.card ∧
                      (1 - 1 / R) ^ (2 * d) * ↑S.card * ↑U.card ≤ ↑(EuclideanGeometry.unitDistancePairsCount U)

declarations.docstring:
**Sawin's Lemmas 11–12 / Remarks Proposition 2.3: the totally real tower.**

There exist $rdBound : \mathbb{R}$ and a *single* infinite set $Q$ of rational primes
$q \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ such that for every $N$ one can find a totally real number field $F/\mathbb{Q}$
of degree $\ge N$ with bounded root discriminant $|disc F|^{1/[F:\mathbb{Q}]} \le rdBound$ in which
*every* prime $q \in Q$ splits completely.

The load-bearing feature is the quantifier order: $Q$ is fixed *before* $F$, so the same primes
split completely in fields of *unbounded* degree. (For a single fixed $F$, Chebotarev already
gives infinitely many completely split primes $\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, so a per-field statement would
be vacuous.) This uniform splitting in an unbounded tower is the key arithmetic input to the
disproof. It is proved as Lemmas 11–12 of Sawin, [arXiv:2605.20579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20579),
and as Proposition 2.3 of the [Remarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695) paper, via the
Golod–Shafarevich inequality for pro-$2$ groups together with the Hajir–Maire–Ramakrishna (2003)
tower construction.

A "completely split" rational prime $q$ in $F$ is one for which $(q)$ is the product of exactly
$[F:\mathbb{Q}]$ distinct maximal ideals.
references: [erdosproblems.com/90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ rdBound Q,
  Q.Infinite ∧
    (∀ q ∈ Q, Nat.Prime q ∧ q % 4 = 1) ∧
      ∀ (N : ℕ),
        ∃ F x,
          ∃ (x_1 : CharZero F) (x_2 : NumberField F) (_ : NumberField.IsTotallyReal F),
            N ≤ Module.finrank ℚ F ∧
              |↑(NumberField.discr F)| ^ (1 / ↑(Module.finrank ℚ F)) ≤ rdBound ∧
                ∀ q ∈ Q, ∃ factors, factors.card = Module.finrank ℚ F ∧ ∀ p ∈ factors, p.IsMaximal ∧ ↑q ∈ p

This lemma confirms that the set of possible unit distance counts is bounded above, which
ensures that taking the supremum (`sSup`) is a well-defined operation. The trivial upper bound is
the total number of pairs of points, $\binom{n}{2}$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $r\geq 2$ and let $t_r(n)$ be the Turán number (the maximal number of edges in a graph on $n$
vertices with no $K_{r+1}$).

If $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and $m\geq t_r(n)$ edges there exists a clique on $r$ vertices,
say $x_1,\ldots,x_r$, such that $$d(x_1)+\cdots+d(x_r)\geq \frac{2rm}{n}.$$

A conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős. This was conjectured in [Er75] only in the special case $r=3$. Edwards [Ed78] proved the conjecture for $2\leq r\leq 8$ (under the additional assumption that $n\geq r^2$). Faudree [Fa92] proved the conjecture for all $r\geq 2$ provided $n>\frac{r-1}{4}r^2$. The full conjecture was proved by Bollobás and Nikiforov [BoNi05].
references: [erdosproblems.com/904](https://www.erdosproblems.com/904)
[BoEr75] Bollobás, B. and Erdős, P., *Unsolved Problems*. Proc. Fifth British Combinatorial Conf. (1975), 678-680.
[Er75] Erdős, P., *Some recent progress on extremal problems in graph theory*. Congr. Numer. (1975), 3-14.
[Ed78] Edwards, C. S., *Complete subgraphs with largest sum of vertex degrees*. (1978), 293-306.
[Fa92] Faudree, Ralph J., *Complete subgraphs with large degree sums*. J. Graph Theory (1992), 327-334.
[BoNi05] Bollobás, Béla and Nikiforov, Vladimir, *The sum of degrees in cliques*. Electron. J. Combin. (2005), Note 21, 10.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (V : Type u_1) [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj],
    ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc 1 (Erdos904.n V),
      Erdos904.turanNumber (Erdos904.n V) r ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
        ∃ s, G.IsNClique r s ∧ 2 * r * G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Erdos904.n V * ∑ v ∈ s, G.degree v

[ErHa68b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of infinite graphs. (1968), 83--98.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ω : Ordinal.{u}),
  ¬∃ V G,
      Cardinal.mk V = Cardinal.aleph (ω + 1) ∧
        G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 ∧
          ∀ (H : G.Subgraph), Cardinal.mk ↑H.verts = Cardinal.aleph ω → H.coe.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph0

declarations.docstring:
A question of Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal [ErHa68b], who proved that for every finite $k$
there is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_k$ vertices where each subgraph on
less than $\aleph_k$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq \aleph_0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/918](https://www.erdosproblems.com/918)
[ErHa68b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of infinite graphs. (1968), 83--98.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  0 < k →
    ∃ V G,
      Cardinal.mk V = Cardinal.aleph ↑k ∧
        G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 ∧
          ∀ (W : Set V),
            Cardinal.mk ↑W < Cardinal.aleph ↑k → (SimpleGraph.induce W G).chromaticCardinal ≤ Cardinal.aleph0

declarations.docstring: Or even $f(n) < n^{c/\log\log n}$ for some constant $c > 0$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/92](https://www.erdosproblems.com/92)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos92.f n) ≤ ↑n ^ (c / Real.log (Real.log ↑n))

declarations.docstring: Is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{o(1)}$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/92](https://www.erdosproblems.com/92)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑(Erdos92.f n) ≤ ↑n ^ o n

declarations.docstring:
A sanity check to ensure the set of possible `f(n)` values is bounded above. A trivial bound is
`n`, since the points equidistant from any `x` form a subset of the other `n - 1` points.
This ensures `sSup` is well-defined.
references: [erdosproblems.com/92](https://www.erdosproblems.com/92)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), BddAbove (Erdos92.possible_f_values n)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for $k\geq 4$, $f_k(n) \gg \frac{n^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}}{(\log n)^{c_k}}$ for some
constant $c_k>0$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
[erdosproblems.com/920](https://www.erdosproblems.com/920)
[erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
[erdosproblems.com/1104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104)
[GrYa68] Graver, Jack E. and Yackel, James, Some graph theoretic results associated with Ramsey's theorem. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 125--175.
[MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraete, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. arXiv:2306.04007 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ c > 0, (fun n => ↑n ^ (1 - 1 / (↑k - 1)) / Real.log ↑n ^ c) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Erdos920.f k n)

declarations.docstring: It is known that $f_3(n)\asymp (n/\log n)^{1/2}$ (see [erdosproblems.com/1104]).
references: [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
[erdosproblems.com/920](https://www.erdosproblems.com/920)
[erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
[erdosproblems.com/1104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104)
[GrYa68] Graver, Jack E. and Yackel, James, Some graph theoretic results associated with Ramsey's theorem. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 125--175.
[MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraete, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. arXiv:2306.04007 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Erdos920.f 3 n)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun n => (↑n / Real.log ↑n) ^ (1 / 2)

declarations.docstring:
A positive answer to this question would follow from [erdosproblems.com/986]. The known bounds for
that problem imply $f_k(n) \gg \frac{n^{1-\frac{2}{k+1}}}{(\log n)^{c_k}}.$
references: [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
[erdosproblems.com/920](https://www.erdosproblems.com/920)
[erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
[erdosproblems.com/1104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104)

[MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraete, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. arXiv:2306.04007 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ k ≥ 3, ∃ c > 0, (fun n => ↑n ^ (1 - 2 / (↑k + 1)) / Real.log ↑n ^ c) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Erdos920.f k n)

declarations.docstring:
The lower bound $R(4,m) \gg m^3/(\log m)^4$ of Mattheus and Verstraete [MaVe23]
(see [erdosproblems.com/166]) implies $f_4(n) \gg \frac{n^{2/3}}{(\log n)^{4/3}}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
[erdosproblems.com/920](https://www.erdosproblems.com/920)
[erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)

[MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraete, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. arXiv:2306.04007 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑n ^ (2 / 3) / Real.log ↑n ^ (4 / 3)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Erdos920.f 4 n)

declarations.docstring:
Graver and Yackel [GrYa68] proved that
$f_k(n) \ll \left(n\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}.$
references: [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
[erdosproblems.com/920](https://www.erdosproblems.com/920)
[erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
[erdosproblems.com/1104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104)
[GrYa68] Graver, Jack E. and Yackel, James, Some graph theoretic results associated with Ramsey's theorem. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 125--175.
[MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraete, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. arXiv:2306.04007 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ k ≥ 3,
  (fun n => ↑(Erdos920.f k n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n =>
    (↑n * Real.log (Real.log ↑n) / Real.log ↑n) ^ (1 - 1 / (↑k - 1))

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every $k$, there is some $f(k)$ such that if $G$ has chromatic number
$\geq f(k)$ then $G$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number $\geq k$?

This is true, as shown by Rödl [Ro77].
references: [erdosproblems.com/923](https://www.erdosproblems.com/923)
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (1969), 27-35.
[Ro77] Rödl, V., *On the chromatic number of subgraphs of a given graph*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1977), 370-371.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (V : Type u_1) (n : ℕ),
    ∃ k, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V), ↑k ≤ G.chromaticNumber → ∃ H ≤ G, ↑n ≤ H.chromaticNumber ∧ H.CliqueFree 3

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every $r$, there is a $k$ such that
if $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ are disjoint intervals of consecutive integers,
all of length at least $k$, then
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq r}\prod_{m\in I_i}m
$$
is not a perfect power?
references: [erdosproblems.com/930](https://www.erdosproblems.com/930)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ r > 0,
    ∃ k,
      ∀ (I₁ I₂ : Fin r → ℕ),
        (∀ (i : Fin r), 0 < I₁ i ∧ I₁ i + k ≤ I₂ i + 1) →
          (∀ (i j : Fin r), i < j → I₂ i < I₁ j) → ¬Erdos930.IsPower (∏ i, ∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (I₁ i) (I₂ i), m)

declarations.docstring:
Erdos and Selfridge [ErSe75] proved that the product of
consecutive integers is never a power (establishing the case $r=1$).

Theorem 1 from [ErSe75].

It is implied from `erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong`.

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.
references: [erdosproblems.com/930](https://www.erdosproblems.com/930)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 ≤ n → 2 ≤ k → ¬Erdos930.IsPower (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m)

declarations.docstring:
Let $k$, $l$, $n$ be integers such that $k \ge 3$, $l \ge 2$ and $n + k \ge p^{(k)}$,
where $p^{(k)}$ is the least prime satisfying $p^{(k)} \ge k$.
Then there is a prime $p \ge k$ for which $l$ does not divide
the multiplicity of the prime factor $p$ in $(n + 1) \ldots (n + k)$.

Theorem 2 from [ErSe75].

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.
references: [erdosproblems.com/930](https://www.erdosproblems.com/930)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k l n : ℕ),
  3 ≤ k →
    2 ≤ l →
      Erdos930.nextPrime k ≤ n + k →
        ∃ p, k ≤ p ∧ Nat.Prime p ∧ ¬l ∣ (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m).factorization p

declarations.docstring:
Let $k_1 \geq k_2 \geq 3$. Are there only finitely many $n_2\geq n_1 + k_1$
such that
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq k_1}(n_1 + i)\ \text{and}\ \prod_{1\leq j\leq k_2} (n_2 + j)
$$
have the same prime factors?
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ),
    k₂ ≥ 3 →
      k₂ ≤ k₁ →
        {(n₁, n₂) |
            n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
              (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős thought perhaps if the two products have the same factors then
$n_2 > 2(n_1 + k_1)$.
It is an open question whether this is true when allowing a finite number of counterexamples.
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ),
    k₂ ≥ 3 →
      k₂ ≤ k₁ →
        {(n₁, n₂) |
            n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
              n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
                (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite

declarations.docstring: In fact there exist counterexamples, like this one found by AlphaProof.
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ k₁ k₂,
  ∃ (_ : k₂ ≤ k₁) (_ : 3 ≤ k₂),
    {(n₁, n₂) |
        n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
          n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
            (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Nonempty

declarations.docstring:
Erdős was unable to prove that if the two products have the same factors
then there must exist a prime between $n_1$ and $n_2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k₁ k₂ n₁ n₂ : ℕ),
  k₂ ≤ k₁ →
    3 ≤ k₂ →
      n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ →
        (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors →
          ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n₁ ≤ p ∧ p ≤ n₂

declarations.docstring:
Let $p_k$ denote the $k$th prime. For infinitely many $r$ there are at least two
integers $p_r < n < p_{r+1}$ all of whose prime factors are $< p_{r + 1} - p_r$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/932](https://www.erdosproblems.com/932)
declarations.type_pretty:
{r |
    2 ≤
      {m ∈ Finset.Ioo (Nat.nth Nat.Prime r) (Nat.nth Nat.Prime r.succ) |
          m.maxPrimeFac < Nat.nth Nat.Prime r.succ - Nat.nth Nat.Prime r}.card}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: Erdős could show that the density of $r$ such that at least one such $n$ exists is $0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/932](https://www.erdosproblems.com/932)
declarations.type_pretty:
{r |
      1 ≤
        {m ∈ Finset.Ioo (Nat.nth Nat.Prime r) (Nat.nth Nat.Prime r.succ) |
            m.maxPrimeFac < Nat.nth Nat.Prime r.succ - Nat.nth Nat.Prime r}.card}.HasDensity
  0

declarations.docstring:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/933](https://www.erdosproblems.com/933)

[Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) / (↑↑n * ↑(Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er76d] wrote 'it is easy to see' that for infinitely many $n$, $2^k 3^l > n\log n$.

Steinerberger has noted a simple proof of this fact follows from taking $n=2^{3^r}$ for any
integer $r\geq 1$, when $k=3^r$ and $l=r+1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/933](https://www.erdosproblems.com/933)

[Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
declarations.type_pretty: {n | ↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) > ↑n * Real.log ↑n}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: Mahler proved (a more general result that implies in particular) that $2^k3^l<n^{1+o(1)}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/933](https://www.erdosproblems.com/933)

[Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c, c =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) < ↑n ^ (1 + c n)

declarations.docstring: Is $n! + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/936](https://www.erdosproblems.com/936)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => x.factorial + 1

declarations.docstring: Is $n! - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/936](https://www.erdosproblems.com/936)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => x.factorial - 1

declarations.docstring: Is $2^n + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/936](https://www.erdosproblems.com/936)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => 2 ^ x + 1

declarations.docstring: Is $2^n - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/936](https://www.erdosproblems.com/936)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => 2 ^ x - 1

declarations.docstring:
Are there infinitely many four-term arithmetic progressions of coprime powerful numbers?
(A number $n$ is *powerful* if $p \mid n \to p^2 \mid n$; `Nat.Powerful`.)

Erdős [Er76d] asked this; the answer is **yes**: Bajpai, Bennett and Chan [BBC24] proved that
there are infinitely many four-term arithmetic progressions of pairwise coprime powerful numbers.
(Without coprimality this is easy, and by a theorem of Fermat there are no four *squares* in
arithmetic progression.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/937](https://www.erdosproblems.com/937)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {p | Erdos937.IsCoprimePowerfulAP4 p.1 p.2}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Sanity check for `IsCoprimePowerfulAP4`: the progression $0, 1, 2, 3$ is not a valid
example, since $2$ is not powerful.
references: [erdosproblems.com/937](https://www.erdosproblems.com/937)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬Erdos937.IsCoprimePowerfulAP4 0 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $A=\{n_1 < n_2 < \cdots\}$ be the sequence of powerful numbers (if $p\mid n$ then $p^2\mid n$).
Are there only finitely many three-term progressions of consecutive terms $n_k,n_{k+1},n_{k+2}$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/938](https://www.erdosproblems.com/938)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  {P |
      (↑P).IsAPOfLength 3 ∧
        ∃ k, P = {Nat.nth Nat.Powerful k, Nat.nth Nat.Powerful (k + 1), Nat.nth Nat.Powerful (k + 2)}}.Finite

declarations.docstring: If $r≥4$ then can the sum of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers ever be itself $r$-powerful?
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939.Erdos939Sums r).Nonempty

declarations.docstring: Cambie has also found solutions when $r=8$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
declarations.type_pretty: (Erdos939.Erdos939Sums 8).Nonempty

declarations.docstring:
Euler had conjectured that the sum of $k - 1$ many $k$-th powers is never a
$k$-th power, but this is false for $k=5$, as Lander and Parkin [LaPa67] found
$$27^5+84^5+110^5+133^5=144^5$$.

[LaPa67] Lander, L. J. and Parkin, T. R., "A counterexample to Euler's sum of powers conjecture."
  Math. Comp. (1967), 101--103.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ (S : Finset ℕ), S.card = k - 1 → ¬∃ q, ∑ s ∈ S, s ^ k = q ^ k

declarations.docstring:
Cambie has found several examples of the sum of $r - 2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers being itself
$r$-powerful. For example when $r=5$ we have
$$3761^5=2^8\cdot3^{10}\cdot 5^7 + 2^{12}\cdot 23^6 + 11^5\cdot 13^5$$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939.Erdos939Sums r).Nonempty

declarations.docstring:
If $r≥4$ are there infinitely many sums of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers
that are themselves $r$-powerful?
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939.Erdos939Sums r).Infinite

declarations.docstring: Cambie has also found solutions when $r=7$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
declarations.type_pretty: (Erdos939.Erdos939Sums 7).Nonempty

declarations.docstring: Are there infinitely many triples of coprime $3$-powerful numbers $a, b, c$ such that $a + b = c$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {(a, b, c) | {a, b, c}.Coprime ∧ Nat.Full 3 a ∧ Nat.Full 3 b ∧ Nat.Full 3 c ∧ a + b = c}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Let $r \ge 3$. Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most $r$ $r$-powerful numbers
has density $0$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ r ≥ 3, {n | ∃ S, S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring: It is not known if all large integers are the sum of at most $r$-many $r$-powerful numbers.
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ r ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S, S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ x = S.sum

declarations.docstring: Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most three cubes has density $0$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | ∃ S, S.card ≤ 3 ∧ n = (Multiset.map (fun x => x ^ 3) S).sum}.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
Heath-Brown [He88] has proved that all large numbers are the sum of at most three
$2$-powerful numbers.

[He88] Heath-Brown, D. R., Ternary quadratic forms and sums of three square-full numbers. (1988), 137--163.
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S, S.card ≤ 3 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, Nat.Full 2 s) ∧ x = S.sum

declarations.docstring: The set of integers which are the sum of at most two $2$-powerful numbers has density $0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | ∃ S, S.card ≤ 2 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, Nat.Full 2 s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that $h(n) < (\log n)^{c + o(1)}$ and, for infinitely many $n$,
$h(n) > (\log n)^{c - o(1)}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/942](https://www.erdosproblems.com/942)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∃ o,
      o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧

declarations.docstring:
Let $k \ge 4$ and $r\ge 1$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
