declarations.docstring:
Let $k \ge 4$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$?

This was conjectured by Dirac in 1970.
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k 1

declarations.docstring:
Dirac's conjecture was proved, for $k=5$: There exists a graph $G$ with chromatic number $5$, such
that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$, or in other words:
has no critical edge.

[Br92] Brown, Jason I., A vertex critical graph without critical edges. Discrete Math. (1992), 99--101
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G 5 1

declarations.docstring: The case $k=4$ and $r=1$ remains open: Are there $4$-critical graphs without any critical edges?
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G 4 1

declarations.docstring:
Jensen [Je02] gave an construction for $k$-critical graphs without any critical edges for all $k ≥ 5$.

[Je02] Jensen, Tommy R., Dense critical and vertex-critical graphs. Discrete Math. (2002), 63--84.
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 5 ≤ k → ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k 1

declarations.docstring:
Lattanzio [La02] proved there exist $k$-critical graphs without critical edges for all $k$ such that
$k - 1$ is not prime.

[La02] Lattanzio, John J., A note on a conjecture of {D}irac. Discrete Math. (2002), 323--330
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k → ¬Nat.Prime (k - 1) → ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k 1

declarations.docstring:
Martinsson and Steiner [MaSt25] proved for every $r \ge 1$ if $k$ is sufficiently large, depending
on $r$, there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$ such that every vertex is critical,
yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$.

[MaSt25] Martinsson, Anders and Steiner, Raphael, Vertex-critical graphs far from edge-criticality. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2025), 151--157
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r → ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k r

This function was considered by de Bruijn, Erdős, and Turán, who showed that
$\sum_{n<x}f(n)\sim \sum_{n<x}f(n)^2\sim x$. They gave no proofs, but a proof of the (harder) second
claim is given by Gorodetsky here [mathoverflow/508491].

declarations.docstring:
Erdős writes that a 'weaker conjecture which is perhaps not quite inaccessible' is that,
for every $\epsilon>0$, if $x$ is sufficiently large there exists $y<x$ such that
$\pi(x)< \pi(y)+\epsilon \pi(x-y)$. Compare this to [855].
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
[erdosproblems.com/950](https://www.erdosproblems.com/950)
[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
[mathoverflow/508491](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508491)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ y < x, ↑x.primeCounting < ↑y.primeCounting + ε * ↑(x - y).primeCounting

declarations.docstring:
He notes that if $\pi(x)< \pi(y)+O\left(\frac{x-y}{\log x}\right)$ for all $y<x-(\log x)^C$ for
some constant $C>0$ then $f(n)\ll \log\log\log n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
[erdosproblems.com/950](https://www.erdosproblems.com/950)
[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
[mathoverflow/508491](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508491)
declarations.type_pretty:
(∃ C > 0,
    ∃ K > 0,
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∀ (y : ℕ), ↑y < ↑x - Real.log ↑x ^ C → ↑x.primeCounting < ↑y.primeCounting + K * ((↑x - ↑y) / Real.log ↑x)) →
  Erdos950.f =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log (Real.log (Real.log ↑n))

declarations.docstring:
Main conjecture:

$\log k(n) \le (\log n)^{(1/2 + o(1))}$
references: [erdosproblems.com/962](https://www.erdosproblems.com/962)
[Er65] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in number theory. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII (1965), 181-189.
[Er76e] Erdős, P., Problems and results on consecutive integers. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1976), 271-282.
[Tang](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-962/blob/main/On_Erd%C5%91s_Problem_962.pdf)
[Tao](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/962)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ ε,
    (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.log ↑(Erdos962.k n) ≤ (Real.log ↑n).rpow (1 / 2 + ε n)

declarations.docstring:
Tang's lower bound [Tang]:

$\log k(n) \ge (1/\sqrt{2} - o(1)) * \sqrt{\log n * \log \log n}$
references: [erdosproblems.com/962](https://www.erdosproblems.com/962)
[Er65] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in number theory. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII (1965), 181-189.
[Er76e] Erdős, P., Problems and results on consecutive integers. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1976), 271-282.
[Tang](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-962/blob/main/On_Erd%C5%91s_Problem_962.pdf)
[Tao](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/962)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ ε,
  (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (1 / √2 - ε n) * √(Real.log ↑n * Real.log (Real.log ↑n)) ≤ Real.log ↑(Erdos962.k n)

declarations.docstring:
Tao's upper bound [Tao]:

$k(n) \le (1 + o(1)) * n^{1/2}$
references: [erdosproblems.com/962](https://www.erdosproblems.com/962)
[Er65] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in number theory. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII (1965), 181-189.

[Tao](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/962)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ ε, (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos962.k n) ≤ (1 + ε n) * √↑n

declarations.docstring:
Erdős asks in [Er75b] if for every 2-coloring of ℝ, there is an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour.

In [Ko16] Péter Komjáth constructed a counterexample.
The same result was proven independently in [SWCol] by Sokoup and Weiss.
references: [erdosproblems.com/965](https://www.erdosproblems.com/965)
[Er75b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
[HLS17] Hindman, Neil and Leader, Imre and Strauss, Dona, Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals. Abh. Math. Semin. Univ. Hambg. (2017), 275--287.
[Ko16] Komjáth, Péter, A certain 2-coloring of the reals. Real Anal. Exchange (2016), 227--231.
[SWCol] Sokoup Dániel and Weiss, William, Sums and Anti-Ramsey Colourings of ℝ. https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/finset_colouring.pdf
declarations.type_pretty: False ↔ ∀ (f : ℝ → Fin 2), ∃ A, ¬A.Countable ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ∀ c ∈ A, ∀ d ∈ A, a ≠ b → c ≠ d → f (a + b) = f (c + d)

declarations.docstring: In fact, in both [Ko16] and [SWCol] a generalized example for $k$-sums is constructed.
references: [erdosproblems.com/965](https://www.erdosproblems.com/965)
[Er75b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
[HLS17] Hindman, Neil and Leader, Imre and Strauss, Dona, Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals. Abh. Math. Semin. Univ. Hambg. (2017), 275--287.
[Ko16] Komjáth, Péter, A certain 2-coloring of the reals. Real Anal. Exchange (2016), 227--231.
[SWCol] Sokoup Dániel and Weiss, William, Sums and Anti-Ramsey Colourings of ℝ. https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/finset_colouring.pdf
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∀ (f : ℝ → Fin 2),
      ∃ A, ¬A.Countable ∧ ∀ (s t : Finset ℝ), ↑s ⊆ A → ↑t ⊆ A → s.card = k → t.card = k → f (s.sum id) = f (t.sum id)

declarations.docstring: Does the set `{n | u n < u (n+1)}` have positive natural density?
references: [erdosproblems.com/968](https://www.erdosproblems.com/968)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | Erdos968.u n < Erdos968.u (n + 1)}.HasPosDensity

Erdős and Prachar proved that the set `{n | u n > u (n+1)}` has positive natural density
(see [ErPr61]).
references: [erdosproblems.com/968](https://www.erdosproblems.com/968)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | Erdos968.u n > Erdos968.u (n + 1)}.HasPosDensity

references: [erdosproblems.com/968](https://www.erdosproblems.com/968)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | Erdos968.u n > Erdos968.u (n + 1) ∧ Erdos968.u (n + 1) > Erdos968.u (n + 2)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: Erdős asked whether there are infinitely many solutions to `uₙ < uₙ₊₁ < uₙ₊₂`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/968](https://www.erdosproblems.com/968)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | Erdos968.u n < Erdos968.u (n + 1) ∧ Erdos968.u (n + 1) < Erdos968.u (n + 2)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Prachar proved `∑_{pₙ < x} |u (n+1) - u n| ≍ (log x)^2` (see [ErPr61]).

We encode `∑_{pₙ < x}` as a sum over `n < Nat.primeCounting' x` (the number of primes `< x`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/968](https://www.erdosproblems.com/968)
declarations.type_pretty:
(fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.Iio x.primeCounting', |Erdos968.u (n + 1) - Erdos968.u n|) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun x =>
  Real.log ↑x ^ 2

declarations.docstring: Does every convex polygon have a vertex with no other 4 vertices equidistant from it?
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
    A.Nonempty → EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑A → ¬Erdos97.HasNEquidistantProperty 4 A

declarations.docstring:
Erdős also conjectured that there is a $k$ for which every convex polygon has a vertex
with no other $k$ vertices equidistant from it.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ k,
    ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      A.Nonempty → EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑A → ¬Erdos97.HasNEquidistantProperty k A

declarations.docstring:
Erdős originally conjectured this (in [Er46b]) with no 3 vertices equidistant,
but Danzer found a convex polygon on 9 points such that every vertex has three
vertices equidistant from it (but this distance depends on the vertex).
Danzer's construction is explained in [Er87b].

[Er46b] Erdős, P., _On sets of distances of $n$ points_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1946), 248-250.
[Er87b] Erdős, P., _Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry_. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985), 167-177.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ A, A.Nonempty ∧ EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑A ∧ Erdos97.HasNEquidistantProperty 3 A

declarations.docstring:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] have found a convex polygon on 20 points such that
every vertex has three vertices equidistant from it (and this distance is the same for all vertices).

[FiRe92] Fishburn, P. C. and Reeds, J. A., _Unit distances between vertices of a convex polygon_. Comput. Geom. (1992), 81-91.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ A, A.Nonempty ∧ EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑A ∧ Erdos97.HasNUnitDistanceProperty 3 A

declarations.docstring:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] also proved that the smallest $n$ for which there exists
a convex $n$-gon and a cut $\{A, B\}$ of its vertices such that $|\{b \in B : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$
for all $a \in A$, and $|\{a \in A : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$ for all $b \in B$, is $n = 20$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty:
sInf
    {n |
      ∃ V A B,
        n = V.card ∧
          EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑V ∧
            A.Nonempty ∧
              B.Nonempty ∧
                Erdos97.IsCut V A B ∧ Erdos97.HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 B A ∧ Erdos97.HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 A B} =
  20

declarations.docstring:
Let `p(a, d)` be the least prime congruent to `a (mod d)`.
Does there exist a constant `c > 0` such that for all large `d`,
`p(a, d) > (1 + c) * φ(d) * log d` for `≫ φ(d)` many values of `a`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/971](https://www.erdosproblems.com/971)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∃ C > 0,
      ∀ᶠ (d : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        C * ↑d.totient ≤
          ↑{a ∈ Finset.Iio d |
                a.Coprime d ∧ ↑(Erdos971.leastCongruentPrime a d) > (1 + c) * ↑d.totient * Real.log ↑d}.card

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that the statement in `erdos_971` holds for infinitely many values of `d`.

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
references: [erdosproblems.com/971](https://www.erdosproblems.com/971)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∃ C > 0,
    {d |
        C * ↑d.totient ≤
          ↑{a ∈ Finset.Iio d |
                a.Coprime d ∧ ↑(Erdos971.leastCongruentPrime a d) > (1 + c) * ↑d.totient * Real.log ↑d}.card}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that for any `ε > 0` we have `p(a, d) < ε * φ(d) * log d` for `≫_ε φ(d)` many
values of `a` (for all large `d`).

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
references: [erdosproblems.com/971](https://www.erdosproblems.com/971)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ∃ C > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (d : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      C * ↑d.totient ≤
        ↑{a ∈ Finset.Iio d | a.Coprime d ∧ ↑(Erdos971.leastCongruentPrime a d) < ε * ↑d.totient * Real.log ↑d}.card

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős problem 972.**
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $\lfloor p\alpha \rfloor$ is also prime?
references: [erdosproblems.com/972](https://www.erdosproblems.com/972)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ α > 1, Irrational α → (Erdos972.primeSet α).Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist a constant $C>1$ such that, for every $n\geq 2$, there exists a sequence
$z_i\in \mathbb{C}$ with $z_1=1$ and $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$ with
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert < C^{-n}$?

This is Problem 7.3 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.
references: [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
[Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ C > 1,
    ∀ n ≥ 2,
      ∃ z,
        z 1 = 1 ∧
          (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) ∧ ∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-↑n)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős proved (as described on p.35 of [Tu84b]) that such a sequence does exist with
$\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$. Indeed, Erdős' construction gives a value of $C\approx 1.32$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
[Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 1,
  ∀ n ≥ 2,
    ∃ z,
      z 1 = 1 ∧
        (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-↑n)

declarations.docstring:
In [Er92f] (a different) Erdős refines this analysis, proving that if
$M_2=\min_{z_j} \max_{2\leq k\leq n+1} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq n}z_j^k\right\rvert$
where the minimum is taken over all $z_j\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\max \lvert z_j\rvert=1$, then
$(1.746)^{-n} < M_2 < (1.745)^{-n}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
[Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ n ≥ 2,
  ∀ (M_2 : ℝ),
    IsGLB
        {M |
          ∃ z,
            (∀ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ ≤ 1) ∧
              (∃ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ = 1) ∧
                ∃ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 1),
                  M = ‖∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, z j ^ k‖ ∧ ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, z j ^ m‖ ≤ M}
        M_2 →
      1.746 ^ (-↑n) < M_2 ∧ M_2 < 1.745 ^ (-↑n)

declarations.docstring:
Tang notes in the comments that Theorem 6.1 of [Tu84b] implies that, if $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$
for all $i$, then
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert \geq (2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
[Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ f,
  (f =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => 1) ∧
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (z : ℕ → ℂ),
        (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
          ∃ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ ≥ (2 * Real.exp 1) ^ (-(1 + f n) * ↑n)

declarations.docstring:
For an irreducible polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(n) \ge 1$ for sufficiently large $n$,
does there exists a constant $c = c(f) > 0$ such that
$\sum_{n \le x} \tau(f(n)) \approx c \cdot x \log x$?

Note that it is unclear whether the polynomial should have integer coefficients or merely be
integer-valued. We assume the former.
references: [erdosproblems.com/975](https://www.erdosproblems.com/975)
[Va39] van der Corput, J. G., Une in\'egalit\'e{} relative au nombre des diviseurs. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Proc. (1939), 547--553.
[Er52b] Erd\"os, P., On the sum {$\sum^x_{k=1} d(f(k))$}. J. London Math. Soc. (1952), 7--15.
[Ho63] Hooley, Christopher, On the number of divisors of a quadratic polynomial. Acta Math. (1963), 97--114.
[Mc95] McKee, James, On the average number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1995), 389--392.
[Mc97] McKee, James, A note on the number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. (1997), 275--281.
[Mc99] McKee, James, The average number of divisors of an irreducible quadratic polynomial. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1999), 17--22.
[T] T. Tao, Erdos' divisor bound, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/07/23/erdos-divisor-bound/
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (f : Polynomial ℤ),
    f.natDegree ≠ 0 →
      Irreducible f →
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℤ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ Polynomial.eval n f) →
          ∃ c > 0, Filter.Tendsto (fun x => Erdos975.Erdos975Sum f x / (x * Real.log x)) Filter.atTop (nhds c)

declarations.docstring: Lower bound for the growth rate of `Erdos975Sum`, shown in [Va39].
references: [erdosproblems.com/975](https://www.erdosproblems.com/975)
[Va39] van der Corput, J. G., Une in\'egalit\'e{} relative au nombre des diviseurs. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Proc. (1939), 547--553.
[Er52b] Erd\"os, P., On the sum {$\sum^x_{k=1} d(f(k))$}. J. London Math. Soc. (1952), 7--15.
[Ho63] Hooley, Christopher, On the number of divisors of a quadratic polynomial. Acta Math. (1963), 97--114.
[Mc95] McKee, James, On the average number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1995), 389--392.
[Mc97] McKee, James, A note on the number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. (1997), 275--281.
[Mc99] McKee, James, The average number of divisors of an irreducible quadratic polynomial. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1999), 17--22.
[T] T. Tao, Erdos' divisor bound, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/07/23/erdos-divisor-bound/
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : Polynomial ℤ),
  Irreducible f →
    f.natDegree ≠ 0 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℤ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ Polynomial.eval n f) →
        (fun x => x * Real.log x) =O[Filter.atTop] Erdos975.Erdos975Sum f

declarations.docstring: Asymptotics for `Erdos975Sum` with $f(X) = X^2 + 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/975](https://www.erdosproblems.com/975)
[Va39] van der Corput, J. G., Une in\'egalit\'e{} relative au nombre des diviseurs. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Proc. (1939), 547--553.
[Er52b] Erd\"os, P., On the sum {$\sum^x_{k=1} d(f(k))$}. J. London Math. Soc. (1952), 7--15.

declarations.docstring:

$\sum_{n \le x} \tau(n^2 + 1) \sim \frac{3}{\pi} x \log x + O(x)$. See Tao's blog [T].

[Er52b] Erd\"os, P., On the sum {$\sum^x_{k=1} d(f(k))$}. J. London Math. Soc. (1952), 7--15.

[Mc95] McKee, James, On the average number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1995), 389--392.
[Mc97] McKee, James, A note on the number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. (1997), 275--281.
[Mc99] McKee, James, The average number of divisors of an irreducible quadratic polynomial. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1999), 17--22.

declarations.docstring:
When $f$ is an irreducible quadratic polynomial, the question is answered first by Hooley [Ho63].
More compact expression of the constant in terms of Hurwitz class numbers (when $a = 1$)

declarations.docstring:
Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2`, is not equal to a power of `2`, and `f n` has no fixed
`(k - 1)`-th power divisors other than `1`. Then the set of `n` such that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th
power free has positive density, and this is proved in [Ho67].
references: [erdosproblems.com/978](https://www.erdosproblems.com/978)
[Ho67] Hooley, C., On the power free values of polynomials. Mathematika (1967), 21--26.
[Br11] Browning, T. D., Power-free values of polynomials. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2011), 139--150.
[Er53] Erdős, P., Arithmetical properties of polynomials. J. London Math. Soc. (1953), 416--425.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {f : Polynomial ℤ},
  Irreducible f →
    2 < f.natDegree →
      (∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) →
        0 < f.leadingCoeff →
          (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∃ n, ¬↑p ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ Polynomial.eval (↑n) f) →
            {n | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (Polynomial.eval (↑n) f)}.HasPosDensity

declarations.docstring:
If $k>3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), and for all primes $p$ there exists $n$ such that $p^{k-2}\nmid f(n)$,
then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is $(k-2)$-power-free?
references: [erdosproblems.com/978](https://www.erdosproblems.com/978)
[Ho67] Hooley, C., On the power free values of polynomials. Mathematika (1967), 21--26.
[Br11] Browning, T. D., Power-free values of polynomials. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2011), 139--150.
[Er53] Erdős, P., Arithmetical properties of polynomials. J. London Math. Soc. (1953), 416--425.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ {f : Polynomial ℤ},
    Irreducible f →
      f.natDegree > 3 →
        (¬∃ l, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) →
          0 < f.leadingCoeff →
            (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∃ n, ¬↑p ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ Polynomial.eval (↑n) f) →
              {n | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (Polynomial.eval (↑n) f)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: Does `n ^ 4 + 2` represent infinitely many squarefree numbers?

declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | Squarefree (n ^ 4 + 2)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
If $k > 3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is
$(k-2)$-power-free?

This was disproved by the DeepMind prover agent.
references: [erdosproblems.com/978](https://www.erdosproblems.com/978)

declarations.type_pretty:

      f.natDegree > 3 →

declarations.docstring: Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?

declarations.docstring:
Question 1:

Is it true that $\limsup_{k \to \infty} A_k = \infty$?

Erdős [Er64b] remarks it is "easy to see" that $\limsup_k \sup_n |\sum_{j \le n} e(k x_j)| = \infty$.
Erdős [Er65b] later found a "very easy" proof that $A_k \gg \log k$ for infinitely many $k$.
Clunie [Cl67] proved that $A_k \gg k^{1/2}$ for infinitely many $k$, which implies the answer is
yes (Tao independently found a proof). This is Problem 7.21 in [Ha74].
references: [erdosproblems.com/987](https://www.erdosproblems.com/987)

[APSSV26b] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant, [Short proofs in combinatorics, probability, and number theory II](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06609). arXiv:2604.06609 (2026).
[Cl67] Clunie, J., On a problem of Erdős. J. London Math. Soc. (1967), 133--136.
[Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964), 52-65.

[Er65b] Erdős, P., Some remarks on number theory. Israel J. Math. (the actual reference cited by Clunie 1967 as [2]; the erdosproblems.com bibliography points to a different Erdős 1965 paper, "Some recent advances and current problems in number theory" (Lectures on Modern Mathematics III, 1965, 196-244), which does not appear to contain the exponential-sum log-bound proof).
[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Li69] Lindström, B., An inequality for $B_2$-sequences. J. Combinatorial Theory (1969), 211-212.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (x : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ (j : ℕ), x j ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) → Filter.limsup (fun k => Erdos987.A x k) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
**Question 2 (parts.ii)**: Is it possible for $A_k = o(k)$? Yes — there exists a sequence
$(x_n) \in (0, 1)$ and a bound $b(k) = o(k)$ with $A x k \le b k$ eventually. A corollary of
`sqrt_log_upper_bound` (which gives a $\sqrt{k \log k}$ bound) plus the asymptotic
$\sqrt{k \log k} = o(k)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/987](https://www.erdosproblems.com/987)

[APSSV26b] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant, [Short proofs in combinatorics, probability, and number theory II](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06609). arXiv:2604.06609 (2026).
[Cl67] Clunie, J., On a problem of Erdős. J. London Math. Soc. (1967), 133--136.
[Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964), 52-65.

[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Li69] Lindström, B., An inequality for $B_2$-sequences. J. Combinatorial Theory (1969), 211-212.

True ↔
  ∃ x,
    ∃ (_ : ∀ (j : ℕ), x j ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1),
      ∃ b, (b =o[Filter.atTop] fun k => ↑k) ∧ ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos987.A x k ≤ ↑(b k)

under the additional assumption that there are only a finite number of distinct points. Clunie
observed in the Mathscinet review of [Li69] that under this assumption in fact $A_k = \infty$
infinitely often (the version stated here).

declarations.docstring:
Clunie [Cl67] proved that there exists an infinite sequence $\{z_\nu\}$ on the unit circle
with $A_\nu \le \nu$ for all $\nu \ge 1$. Translating $z_\nu = e(x_\nu)$, the natural domain of
$x_\nu$ is the half-open unit interval $\mathrm{Ico}\,0\,1$, matching the original
[Er64b]/[Cl67] statement (any unit complex number is allowed, including $z = 1$, i.e. $x = 0$).

**Note**: erdosproblems.com/987 phrases the problem with the *open* interval
$x_\nu \in (0, 1)$, which excludes $z = 1$ and is strictly stronger than what [Er64b]/[Cl67]
state; we align with the original papers here. The shifted-vdc $\le k + 1$ variant under the
open interval is preserved as `linear_upper_bound_clunie`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/987](https://www.erdosproblems.com/987)

[APSSV26b] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant, [Short proofs in combinatorics, probability, and number theory II](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06609). arXiv:2604.06609 (2026).
[Cl67] Clunie, J., On a problem of Erdős. J. London Math. Soc. (1967), 133--136.
[Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964), 52-65.

[Er65b] Erdős, P., Some remarks on number theory. Israel J. Math. (the actual reference cited by Clunie 1967 as [2]; the erdosproblems.com bibliography points to a different Erdős 1965 paper, "Some recent advances and current problems in number theory" (Lectures on Modern Mathematics III, 1965, 196-244), which does not appear to contain the exponential-sum log-bound proof).
[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Li69] Lindström, B., An inequality for $B_2$-sequences. J. Combinatorial Theory (1969), 211-212.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ x, ∃ (_ : ∀ (j : ℕ), x j ∈ Set.Ico 0 1), ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → Erdos987.A x k ≤ ↑↑k

declarations.docstring:
**Linear upper bound (tight via Clunie phase tracking).** Tighter than
`linear_upper_bound_weak`: there exists a sequence $x \in (0,1)$ with $A_k \le k + 1$ for all
$k \ge 1$, via the (shifted) van der Corput sequence. Whether the $+1$ can be eliminated to
recover Clunie's exact $A_k \le k$ under the strict $\mathrm{Ioo}\,0\,1$ hypothesis is open in
this formalization (see `linear_upper_bound`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/987](https://www.erdosproblems.com/987)

[APSSV26b] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant, [Short proofs in combinatorics, probability, and number theory II](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06609). arXiv:2604.06609 (2026).
[Cl67] Clunie, J., On a problem of Erdős. J. London Math. Soc. (1967), 133--136.
[Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964), 52-65.

[Er65b] Erdős, P., Some remarks on number theory. Israel J. Math. (the actual reference cited by Clunie 1967 as [2]; the erdosproblems.com bibliography points to a different Erdős 1965 paper, "Some recent advances and current problems in number theory" (Lectures on Modern Mathematics III, 1965, 196-244), which does not appear to contain the exponential-sum log-bound proof).
[Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
[Li69] Lindström, B., An inequality for $B_2$-sequences. J. Combinatorial Theory (1969), 211-212.

declarations.docstring:
**Linear upper bound (weakened).** A first weakened version of Clunie's `A_k ≤ k`: there
exists a sequence $x \in (0,1)$ with $A_k \le 2k$ for all $k \ge 1$. The witness is the
(shifted) van der Corput sequence. For the tighter $A_k \le k + 1$ bound see

An internal OpenAI model (see [APSSV26b, §3]) proved that there exists an infinite sequence
$x_1, x_2, \ldots \in (0, 1)$ such that
$\sup_n \left\lvert \sum_{j \le n} e(k x_j) \right\rvert \ll (k \log k)^{1/2}$ for all $k \ge 1$
(in particular $A_k \ll (k \log k)^{1/2}$).

Note: the bound is restricted to $k \ge 2$ since $\log 1 = 0$ would make the RHS vanish at
$k = 1$, while the LHS $\|\sum_{j < n} e(x_j)\|$ can equal $1$ (e.g. for $n = 1$).

declarations.docstring:
Does there exists a positive constant `C` such that for all `f ∈ L²[0,1]` and all lacunary
sequences `n`, if `‖f - fₖ‖₂ = O(1 / log log log k ^ C)`, then for almost every `x`,
`lim ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, f (n k • x)) / N = ∫ t, f t ∂t`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/996](https://www.erdosproblems.com/996)
[Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
[Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal, Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ C,
    0 < C ∧
      ∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℂ 2 AddCircle.haarAddCircle)) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
        IsLacunary n →
          ((fun k =>
                (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (Erdos996.fourierPartial f k) 2 AddCircle.haarAddCircle).toReal) =O[Filter.atTop]
              fun k => 1 / Real.log (Real.log (Real.log ↑k)) ^ C) →
            ∀ᵐ (x : AddCircle 1),
              Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, ↑↑f (n k • x)) / ↑N) Filter.atTop
                (nhds (∫ (t : AddCircle 1), ↑↑f t ∂AddCircle.haarAddCircle))

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every $\alpha$, the sequence $\{ \alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed,
if $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

The answer is yes, by [APSSV26, Section 4]; a Lean formalisation is available in [Mo26].
references: [erdosproblems.com/997](https://www.erdosproblems.com/997)
[APSSV26] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant, [Short proofs in combinatorics and number theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29961). arXiv:2603.29961 (2026).

declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (α : ℝ), ¬Erdos997.IsWellDistributed fun n => Int.fract (α * ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Prime n))

declarations.docstring:
He also claimed in [Er64b] to have proved that there exists an irrational $\alpha$ for which
$\{\alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed. He later retracted this claim in [Er85e], saying "The
theorem is no doubt correct and perhaps will not be difficult to prove but I never was able to
reconstruct my 'proof' which perhaps never existed."

The existence of such an $\alpha$ was established by Champagne, Le, Liu, and Wooley [CLLW24].

declarations.docstring:
Euler's sum of powers conjecture states that for integers $n > 1$ and $k > 1$,
if the sum of $n$ positive integers each raised to the $k$-th power equals another integer
raised to the $k$-th power, then $n ≥ k$.

The conjecture is known to be false for $k = 4$ and $k = 5$,
but remains open for $k ≥ 6$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler's_sum_of_powers_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n k b : ℕ), 1 < n → 5 < k → ∀ (a : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ (i : Fin n), a i > 0) → ∑ i, a i ^ k = b ^ k → k ≤ n

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler's_sum_of_powers_conjecture)

declarations.docstring:
The **Fermat–Catalan conjecture** states that the equation
$a^m + b^n = c^k$ has only finitely many solutions $(a,b,c,m,n,k)$ with distinct triplets of values
$(a^m, b^n, c^k)$ where $a, b, c$ are positive coprime integers and $m, n, k$ are positive integers satisfying
$\frac 1 m + \frac 1 n + \frac 1 k < 1$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat-Catalan_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: FermatCatalanConjecture.fermatCatalanConjecture

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat-Catalan_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (m n k : ℕ),
  0 < m →
    0 < n →
      0 < k →
        1 / ↑m + 1 / ↑n + 1 / ↑k < 1 →
          {(a, b, c) | 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ 0 < c ∧ a ^ m + b ^ n = c ^ k ∧ {a, b, c}.Pairwise Nat.Coprime}.Finite

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_prime)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | (∃ m, Nat.fib m = n) ∧ Nat.Prime n}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: There are infinitely many indices $i$, such that the $i$-th Fibonacci is prime.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_prime)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | Nat.Prime (Nat.fib n)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: The two ways of phrasing the conjecture are equivalent.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_prime)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | Nat.Prime (Nat.fib n)}.Infinite ↔ {n | (∃ m, Nat.fib m = n) ∧ Nat.Prime n}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
**Firoozbakht's conjecture**
The inequality $\sqrt[n+1]{p_{n+1}} < \sqrt[n]{p_n}$ holds for all prime numbers $p_n$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firoozbakht%27s_conjecture)
[primepuzzles](https://www.primepuzzles.net/conjectures/conj_030.htm)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Firoozbakht.firoozbakhtSeq (n + 1) < Firoozbakht.firoozbakhtSeq n

declarations.docstring:
The inequality $p_{n+1}-p_n < (\log p_n)^2-\log p_n$ holds for all $n>4$.
A consequence of Firuzbakht's conjecture.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firoozbakht%27s_conjecture)
[primepuzzles](https://www.primepuzzles.net/conjectures/conj_030.htm)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  3 < n →
    (∀ (n : ℕ), Firoozbakht.firoozbakhtSeq (n + 1) < Firoozbakht.firoozbakhtSeq n) →
      ↑(Nat.nth Prime (n + 1)) - ↑(Nat.nth Prime n) < Real.log ↑(Nat.nth Prime n) ^ 2 - Real.log ↑(Nat.nth Prime n)

declarations.docstring: The Cookson Hills series summing $sec(n)^2 / n^3$ from $n=1$ to $\infty$ converges.
references: [Wikipedia: Examples of numerical series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_(mathematics)#Examples_of_numerical_series)
[MathWorld: Flint Hills Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/FlintHillsSeries.html)

[MathWorld: Cookson Hills Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/CooksonHillsSeries.html)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Summable fun n => 1 / ((↑n + 1) ^ 3 * Real.cos (↑n + 1) ^ 2)

declarations.docstring:
The Flint Hills series summing $csc(n)^2 / n^3$ from $n=1$ to $\infty$ converges.
(Note that we 0-index the series below.)
references: [Wikipedia: Examples of numerical series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_(mathematics)#Examples_of_numerical_series)

[MathWorld: Cookson Hills Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/CooksonHillsSeries.html)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Summable fun n => 1 / ((↑n + 1) ^ 3 * Real.sin (↑n + 1) ^ 2)

declarations.docstring: **Fuglede's conjecture** in one dimension: A bounded subset of ℝ with positive Lebesgue measure is spectral iff it tiles ℝ by translation.
references: [Fuglede's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuglede%27s_conjecture)

declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Fuglede.FugledeConjectureFor 2

(Note that counterexamples in lower dimensions would also disprove the conjecture in higher dimensions.)

declarations.docstring:
If `x` is a fusible number and `y` is its successor, then the interval `[x + 1, y + 1)` can be
divided into intervals `[ℓₙ, ℓₙ₊₁)`, such that the fusible numbers in `[ℓₙ, ℓₙ₊₁)` are obtained by
fusing the `n + 1`st successor of `x` with a fusible number.
This formalization differs from Conjecture 7.1 in the paper in four ways:
(1) it is obtained from Conjecture 7.1 by plugging in `n + 1` into `n`, which simplifies the expressions
  and removes the need to assume `n ≥ 1`;
(2) the `n + 1`st successor `s^(n+1)(x)` is replaced by the explicit value `x + (2 - 1 / 2 ^ n) * m`;
(3) instead of defining `y` to be the successor of `x`, we assert that there is no fusible number
  strictly between `x` and `y`;
(4) instead of using `∃ z, IsFusible z ∧ q = s^(n+1)(x) ~ z` we use the value of `z` determined by the equality,
  namely `z = 2 * q - 1 - s^(n+1)(x)`, and it is easy to see `z ∈ [x + 1 - m / 2 ^ n, x + 1)` as required.
references: [Fusible numbers and Peano Arithmetic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.14342), by Jeff Erickson, Gabriel Nivasch, and Junyan Xu.
[Fusible numbers and Peano Arithmetic](https://doi.org/10.46298/lmcs-18%283%3A6%292022), Logical Methods in Computer Science, Volume 18, Issue 3 (July 28, 2022).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (x y q : ℚ) (n : ℕ),
  FusibleNumber.IsFusible x →
    FusibleNumber.IsFusible y →
      x < y →
        (∀ (z : ℚ), FusibleNumber.IsFusible z → z ∉ Set.Ioo x y) →
          have m := y - x;
          have ℓ := fun n => y + 1 - m / 2 ^ n;
          FusibleNumber.IsFusible q →
            q ∈ Set.Ico (ℓ n) (ℓ (n + 1)) → FusibleNumber.IsFusible (2 * q - 1 - x - (2 - 1 / 2 ^ n) * m)

declarations.docstring: The rational number $1$ is fusible.
references: [Fusible numbers and Peano Arithmetic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.14342), by Jeff Erickson, Gabriel Nivasch, and Junyan Xu.

declarations.type_pretty: FusibleNumber.IsFusible 1

declarations.docstring:
The **Generalized Riemann Hypothesis** asserts that all the non-trivial zeros of the
Dirichlet $L$-function $L(\chi, s)$ of a primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ have real part
$\frac{1}{2}$.
references: [The Clay Institute](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf)
[Wikipedia: Riemann hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemann_hypothesis)
[Wikipedia: Generalized Riemann hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_Riemann_hypothesis)
[Wikipedia: Dedekind zeta function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dedekind_zeta_function)
J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Springer (Grundlehren 322), 1999, Chapter VII, §5.
D. A. Marcus, *Number Fields*, Springer (GTM 81), 1977, Chapter VII.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (q : ℕ) [inst : NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q),
  χ.IsPrimitive → ∀ (s : ℂ), DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s = 0 → s ∉ Int.cast '' GRH.trivialZeros χ → s.re = 1 / 2

declarations.docstring: GRH for $\chi = 1$ is `RiemannHypothesis`.
references: [The Clay Institute](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf)
[Wikipedia: Riemann hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemann_hypothesis)
[Wikipedia: Generalized Riemann hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_Riemann_hypothesis)
[Wikipedia: Dedekind zeta function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dedekind_zeta_function)
J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Springer (Grundlehren 322), 1999, Chapter VII, §5.
D. A. Marcus, *Number Fields*, Springer (GTM 81), 1977, Chapter VII.
declarations.type_pretty:
(DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive 1 →
    ∀ (s : ℂ), DirichletCharacter.LFunction 1 s = 0 → s ∉ Int.cast '' GRH.trivialZeros 1 → s.re = 1 / 2) ↔
  RiemannHypothesis

declarations.docstring:
If a finitely generated group has superpolynomial growth, then with respect to any finite
generating set its growth function is at least $e^{\sqrt n}$ in Grigorchuk's preorder on
growth functions, where the comparison is witnessed by linearly rescaling the radius.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gromov%27s_theorem_on_groups_of_polynomial_growth#The_gap_conjecture)
[On the Gap Conjecture concerning group growth](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1202.6044) by *Rostislav Grigorchuk*
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (G : Type) [inst : Group G] (S : Set G),
  S.Finite →
    Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ →
      GromovPolynomialGrowth.HasSuperPolynomialGrowth G →
        ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.exp √↑n ≤ ↑(GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction S (C * n))

declarations.docstring:
It is conjectured that the correct bound is
$$
  |E(r)| = O\left(r^{1/2 + o(1)}\right)
$$

[Ha59]  Hardy, G. H. (1959). _Ramanujan: Twelve Lectures on Subjects Suggested by His Life and Work_(3rd ed.). New York: Chelsea Publishing Company. p. 67

See also https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03549
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauss_circle_problem)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ o, ∃ (_ : Filter.Tendsto o Filter.atTop (nhds 0)), GaussCircleProblem.E =O[Filter.atTop] fun r => r ^ (1 / 2 + o r)

declarations.docstring:
Gauss proved that
$$
  |E(r)|\leq 2\sqrt{2}\pi r,
$$
for sufficiently large $r$.

[Ha59]  Hardy, G. H. (1959). _Ramanujan: Twelve Lectures on Subjects Suggested by His Life and Work_(3rd ed.). New York: Chelsea Publishing Company. p. 67
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauss_circle_problem)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (r : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, |GaussCircleProblem.E r| ≤ 2 * √2 * Real.pi * r

declarations.docstring:
Hardy and Laundau independently found a lower bound by showing that
$$
  |E(r)| \neq o\left(r^{1/2}(\log r)^{1/4}\right)
$$
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauss_circle_problem)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬GaussCircleProblem.E =o[Filter.atTop] fun r => √r * √√(Real.log r)

declarations.docstring:
The value of $N(r)$ can be expressed as
$$
  N(r) = 1 + 4\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\left(\left\lfloor\frac{r^2}{4i+1}\right\rfloor -
    \left\lfloor\frac{r^2}{4i + 3}\right\rfloor\right).
$$
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauss_circle_problem)

declarations.docstring:
**Gilbreath's conjecture**
Gilbreath's conjecture states that every term in the sequence $d^k_0$ for $k > 0$ is equal to 1.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbreath%27s_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ+), Gilbreath.d (↑k) 0 = 1

declarations.docstring: Can every even integer greater than 2 be written as the sum of two primes?
references: [Landau Problems Wikipedia Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landau%27s_problems#Twin_prime_conjecture)
[Goldbach's Conjecture Wikipedia Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldbach%27s_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 < n → Even n → ∃ p q, Prime p ∧ Prime q ∧ n = p + q

declarations.docstring:
**Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture** (1973): every group is surjunctive.
That is, for every group `G` and every finite alphabet `A`, every injective cellular
automaton on `A^G` is surjective.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surjunctive_group)
Gottschalk, W. H. (1973), "Some general dynamical notions"
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (G : Type) [inst : Group G], GottschalkSurjunctivity.IsSurjunctive G

declarations.docstring:
Every finite group is surjunctive. This is a classical result: an injective
endomorphism of a finite set is surjective.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surjunctive_group)
Gottschalk, W. H. (1973), "Some general dynamical notions"
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (G : Type) [inst : Group G] [Finite G], GottschalkSurjunctivity.IsSurjunctive G

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surjunctive_group)
Gottschalk, W. H. (1973), "Some general dynamical notions"
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] {A : Type u_2} (g : G) (x : G → A) (h : G),
  GottschalkSurjunctivity.shift G g x h = x (g⁻¹ * h)

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surjunctive_group)
Gottschalk, W. H. (1973), "Some general dynamical notions"
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] {A : Type u_2} (g₁ g₂ : G) (x : G → A),
  GottschalkSurjunctivity.shift G (g₁ * g₂) x =
    GottschalkSurjunctivity.shift G g₁ (GottschalkSurjunctivity.shift G g₂ x)

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surjunctive_group)
Gottschalk, W. H. (1973), "Some general dynamical notions"
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] {A : Type u_2} (x : G → A), GottschalkSurjunctivity.shift G 1 x = x

declarations.docstring:
The Gourevitch series identity:
The following idenitity holds:
$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1 + 14 n + 76 n^2 + 168 n^3}{2^{20 n}} \binom{2n}{n}^7 = \frac{32}{\pi^3}.$
This was originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera and proven in [A2025] by Au.
references: [About a New Kind of Ramanujan-Type Series](https://doi.org/10.1080/10586458.2003.10504518) by *Jesús Guillera*
[G2003] Guillera, Jesús. "About a new kind of Ramanujan-type series." Experimental Mathematics 12.4 (2003): 507-510.
[A2025] Au, Kam Cheong. "Wilf-Zeilberger seeds and non-trivial hypergeometric identities." Journal of Symbolic Computation 130 (2025): 102421. [arXiv:2312.14051](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14051)

declarations.docstring:
Every tree admits a graceful labeling.

A graceful labeling of a tree $T$ with $m$ edges is an injective map $f : V \to \{0, \dots, m\}$
such that the multiset of absolute differences $|f(u) - f(v)|$ over edges $\{u,v\}$ of $T$
equals $\{1, \dots, m\}$.
references: [Wikipedia/Graceful_labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (T : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel T.Adj],
  T.IsTree →
    have m := T.edgeFinset.card;
    ∃ f,
      Function.Injective f ∧
        (∀ (v : V), f v ≤ m) ∧
          Finset.image (fun e => Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => (↑(f u) - ↑(f v)).natAbs, ⋯⟩ e) T.edgeFinset = Finset.Icc 1 m

references: [Wikipedia/Graceful_labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)
[Wikipedia/Graceful_labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be a set of $n$ positive integers. Does $A$ contain a sum-free set
of size at least $\frac n 3 + Ω(n)$, where $Ω(n) → ∞$ as $n → ∞$?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 1](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.1 Problem 1)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ Ω,
    Filter.Tendsto Ω Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ), (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) → A.card = n → ∃ S ⊆ A, IsSumFree ↑S ∧ ↑n / 3 + Ω n ≤ ↑S.card

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be an abelian group of size $N$, and suppose that $A \subset G$ has density $\alpha$.
Are there at least $\alpha^{15} N^{10}$ tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_5, y_1, \dots, y_5) \in G^{10}$
such that $x_i + y_j \in A$ whenever $j \in \{i, i+1, i+2\}$?

Note: We interpret indices modulo 5.

declarations.docstring:
Is $W(k, r)$ a polynomial in $r$, for fixed $k$?

We formulate this as asking if $W(k, r)$ has polynomial growth in $r$.
We know it is not the case for $k = 3$ [Gr21, p.3].

declarations.docstring: What is the largest subset of $[N]$ with no solution to $x + 3y = 2z + 2w$ in distinct integers $x, y, z, w$?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 16](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.16)

[Yufei Zhao](Via Personal Communication with Ben Green)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (N : ℕ),
  ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
    Green16.SolutionFree A ∧
      A.card = sorry ∧ MaximalFor (fun B => B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ Green16.SolutionFree B) Finset.card A

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $G$ is a finite group, and let $A \subset G \times G$ be a subset of density $\alpha$.
Is it true that there are $\gg_\alpha |G|^3$ triples $x, y, g$ such that $(x, y), (gx, y), (x, gy)$
all lie in $A$?

Note: A is taken as $\alpha$-dense, i.e. $|A| \ge \alpha |G|^2$ [Au16, Question 2]
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problem 18](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.18)
[Au16] Austin, Tim. "Ajtai–Szemerédi theorems over quasirandom groups." Recent trends in combinatorics. Cham: Springer International Publishing, 2016. 453-484.
[So13] Solymosi, Jozsef. "Roth-type theorems in finite groups." European Journal of Combinatorics 34.8 (2013): 1454-1458.
[Go01] Gowers, William T. "A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 11.3 (2001): 465-588.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ α > 0,
    ∃ c > 0,
      ∃ m₀,
        ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Fintype G] [inst_2 : DecidableEq G] (A : Finset (G × G)),
          Fintype.card G ≥ m₀ →
            ↑A.card ≥ α * ↑(Fintype.card G) ^ 2 → ↑(Green18.numNaiveCorners A) ≥ c * ↑(Fintype.card G) ^ 3

declarations.docstring: [So13] proved this is true for "BMZ corners". Follows from the proof of Theorem 2.1, p.1456-1457.
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problem 18](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.18)
[Au16] Austin, Tim. "Ajtai–Szemerédi theorems over quasirandom groups." Recent trends in combinatorics. Cham: Springer International Publishing, 2016. 453-484.
[So13] Solymosi, Jozsef. "Roth-type theorems in finite groups." European Journal of Combinatorics 34.8 (2013): 1454-1458.
[Go01] Gowers, William T. "A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 11.3 (2001): 465-588.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ α > 0,
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∃ m₀,
      ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Fintype G] [inst_2 : DecidableEq G] (A : Finset (G × G)),
        Fintype.card G ≥ m₀ →
          ↑A.card ≥ α * ↑(Fintype.card G) ^ 2 → ↑(Green18.numBmzCorners A) ≥ c * ↑(Fintype.card G) ^ 3

declarations.docstring:
What is $C$, the infimum of all exponents $c$ for which the following is true, uniformly for
$0 < \alpha < 1$? Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n \times \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density
$\alpha$. Write $N := 2^n$. Then there is some $d \neq 0$ such that $A$ contains $\gg \alpha^c N^2$
corners $(x,y), (x,y+d), (x+d,y)$.

This question has been resolved by [FSS20], showing that $C = 4$.
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.19)
[FSS20] Fox, Jacob, et al. "Triforce and corners." Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society. Vol. 169. No. 1. Cambridge University Press, 2020.
[Ma21] Mandache, Matei. "A variant of the Corners theorem." Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society. Vol. 171. No. 3. Cambridge University Press, 2021.
[Ch11] Chu, Qing. "Multiple recurrence for two commuting transformations." Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems 31.3 (2011): 771-792.
declarations.type_pretty: Green19.C = 4

declarations.docstring: [Ma21] showed that $3.13 \leq C$.
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.19)
[FSS20] Fox, Jacob, et al. "Triforce and corners." Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society. Vol. 169. No. 1. Cambridge University Press, 2020.
[Ma21] Mandache, Matei. "A variant of the Corners theorem." Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society. Vol. 171. No. 3. Cambridge University Press, 2021.
[Ch11] Chu, Qing. "Multiple recurrence for two commuting transformations." Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems 31.3 (2011): 771-792.
declarations.type_pretty: Green19.C ≥ 3.13

declarations.docstring: [Ma21] showed that $C \leq 4$.
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.19)
[FSS20] Fox, Jacob, et al. "Triforce and corners." Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society. Vol. 169. No. 1. Cambridge University Press, 2020.
[Ma21] Mandache, Matei. "A variant of the Corners theorem." Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society. Vol. 171. No. 3. Cambridge University Press, 2021.
[Ch11] Chu, Qing. "Multiple recurrence for two commuting transformations." Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems 31.3 (2011): 771-792.
declarations.type_pretty: Green19.C ≤ 4

declarations.docstring:
Let $A \subset \mathbf{Z}$ be a set of $n$ integers. Is there a set $S \subset A$ of size
$(\log n)^{100}$ such that the restricted sumset$S \hat{+} S$ is disjoint from $A$?
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset ℤ), A.card = n → ↑(Green2.maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A) ≥ Real.log ↑n ^ 100

declarations.docstring: From [Sa21] it is known that there is always such an S with $|S| \gt (\log |A|)^{1+c}$.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset ℤ), A.card = n → ↑(Green2.maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A) ≥ Real.log ↑n ^ (1 + c)

declarations.docstring: From [Ch71] it is known that $M(A) \le |A|^{2/5 + o(1)}$.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ o,
  ∃ (_ : Filter.Tendsto o Filter.atTop (nhds 0)),
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ A, A.card = n ∧ ↑(Green2.maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A) ≤ ↑A.card ^ (2 / 5 + o A.card)

declarations.docstring: From [Er65] it is known that $M(A) \le \frac{1}{3}|A| + O(1)$.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ A, A.card = n ∧ ↑(Green2.maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A) ≤ ↑A.card / 3 + C

declarations.docstring: From [Ru05] the best-known upper bound is $|S| \lt e^{C \sqrt{\log |A|}}$.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ A, A.card = n ∧ ↑(Green2.maxRestrictedSumAvoidingSubsetSize A) < Real.exp (C * √(Real.log ↑A.card))

declarations.docstring:
If $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ is $r$-coloured then, for $N \geqslant N_0(r)$, there are integers
$x, y \geqslant 3$ such that $x + y, xy$ have the same colour.

Find reasonable bounds for $N_0(r)$. The goal is to improve upon the Green-Sawhney bound.
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.22)
[Mo17] Moreira, Joel. "Monochromatic sums and products in N." Annals of Mathematics 185.3 (2017): 1069-1090.
[GrSa25] Green, Ben, and Mehtaab Sawhney. "Bounds for monochromatic solutions to $\{x+ y, xy\} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.09365 (2025).
[Ri25] Richter, Florian K. "Sums and products in sets of positive density." arXiv preprint arXiv:2507.00515 (2025).
[BoSa24] Bowen, Matt, and Marcin Sabok. "Monochromatic products and sums in the rationals." Forum of Mathematics, Pi. Vol. 12. Cambridge University Press, 2024.
[Bo25] Bowen, Matt. "Monochromatic products and sums in 2-colorings of N." Advances in Mathematics 462 (2025): 110095.
[Al23] Alweiss, Ryan. "Monochromatic Sums and Products over $\mathbb {Q} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2307.08901 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty:
have ans := sorry;
∀ᶠ (r : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Green22.N₀ r) ≤ ans r ∧ ans =o[Filter.atTop] Green22.GreenSawhneyBound

declarations.docstring: [GrSa25, Theorem 1.1] found a permissible upper bound.
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.22)
[Mo17] Moreira, Joel. "Monochromatic sums and products in N." Annals of Mathematics 185.3 (2017): 1069-1090.
[GrSa25] Green, Ben, and Mehtaab Sawhney. "Bounds for monochromatic solutions to $\{x+ y, xy\} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.09365 (2025).
[Ri25] Richter, Florian K. "Sums and products in sets of positive density." arXiv preprint arXiv:2507.00515 (2025).
[BoSa24] Bowen, Matt, and Marcin Sabok. "Monochromatic products and sums in the rationals." Forum of Mathematics, Pi. Vol. 12. Cambridge University Press, 2024.
[Bo25] Bowen, Matt. "Monochromatic products and sums in 2-colorings of N." Advances in Mathematics 462 (2025): 110095.
[Al23] Alweiss, Ryan. "Monochromatic Sums and Products over $\mathbb {Q} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2307.08901 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (r : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Green22.N₀ r) ≤ Green22.GreenSawhneyBound r

declarations.docstring:
Since $x, y \geq 3$, we must have $xy \geq 9$, so $N_0(r) \geq 9$
(assuming $N_0(r)$ is well-defined, which follows from [Mo17]).
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.22)
[Mo17] Moreira, Joel. "Monochromatic sums and products in N." Annals of Mathematics 185.3 (2017): 1069-1090.

[Ri25] Richter, Florian K. "Sums and products in sets of positive density." arXiv preprint arXiv:2507.00515 (2025).
[BoSa24] Bowen, Matt, and Marcin Sabok. "Monochromatic products and sums in the rationals." Forum of Mathematics, Pi. Vol. 12. Cambridge University Press, 2024.

[Al23] Alweiss, Ryan. "Monochromatic Sums and Products over $\mathbb {Q} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2307.08901 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (r : ℕ), r ≠ 0 → 9 ≤ Green22.N₀ r

declarations.docstring:
[Mo17, Corollary 1.5] For any finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist (infinitely many)
$x, y \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\{xy, x + y\}$ is monochromatic.

This guarantees that $N_0(r)$ is well-defined.

Note: [Mo17] also establishes that $x$ is of the same colour.
references: [Gr26] [Ben Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.22)
[Mo17] Moreira, Joel. "Monochromatic sums and products in N." Annals of Mathematics 185.3 (2017): 1069-1090.
[GrSa25] Green, Ben, and Mehtaab Sawhney. "Bounds for monochromatic solutions to $\{x+ y, xy\} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.09365 (2025).
[Ri25] Richter, Florian K. "Sums and products in sets of positive density." arXiv preprint arXiv:2507.00515 (2025).
[BoSa24] Bowen, Matt, and Marcin Sabok. "Monochromatic products and sums in the rationals." Forum of Mathematics, Pi. Vol. 12. Cambridge University Press, 2024.
[Bo25] Bowen, Matt. "Monochromatic products and sums in 2-colorings of N." Advances in Mathematics 462 (2025): 110095.
[Al23] Alweiss, Ryan. "Monochromatic Sums and Products over $\mathbb {Q} $." arXiv preprint arXiv:2307.08901 (2023).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ) (coloring : ℕ → Fin r),
  {p | 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ coloring p.1 = coloring (p.1 * p.2) ∧ coloring p.1 = coloring (p.1 + p.2)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $\mathbb{N}$ is finitely coloured. Are there $x,y$ of the same colour such that $x^2 +
y^2$ is a square?

Solved in [FrKlMo25].
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ) (c : ℕ → Fin k), ∃ x y, 0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧ c x = c y ∧ IsSquare (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2)

declarations.docstring:
If $A$ is a set of $n$ integers, what is the maximum number of affine translates of the set
$\lbrace 0,1,3 \rbrace$ that $A$ can contain?

Conjectured in [Aa19] p.579: $\left({1}{3} + o(1)\right) n^2$.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Green24.max013AffineTranslates n = sorry

declarations.docstring: Conjecture p.579 in [Aa19]: $\left({1}{3} + o(1)\right) n^2$.
declarations.type_pretty: Green24.variants.gamma = 1 / 3

declarations.docstring: Asymptotic lower bound (1.2) in [Aa19]. Named after Hardy and Littlewood [HaL28].
declarations.type_pretty: Green24.variants.gamma ≥ 1 / 12

declarations.docstring: Asymptotic upper bound (1.2) in [Aa19]. Named after Hardy and Littlewood [HaL28].
declarations.type_pretty: Green24.variants.gamma ≤ 3 / 4

declarations.docstring: From [Aa19] p.577: the trivial upper bound is $n^2$ (non asymptotic).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, Green24.max013AffineTranslates n ≤ n ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
For which values of $k$ is the following true: whenever we partition $[N] = A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_k$,
$\left|\bigcup^k_{i=1} (A_i \hat{+} A_i)\right| \geq \frac{1}{10} N$?
declarations.type_pretty: {k | ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Green25.Property25 (k N) N} = sorry

declarations.docstring: We conjecture that the best-known lower bound can be raised.
declarations.type_pretty:
have ans := sorry;
Green25.bestLower =o[Filter.atTop] ans ∧
  (∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ ans N ∧ ans N ≤ ↑N) ∧
    ∀ (k : ℕ → ℕ),
      (∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ k N ∧ k N ≤ N) ∧ (fun N => ↑(k N)) =O[Filter.atTop] ans →
        ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Green25.Property25 (k N) N

declarations.docstring: We conjecture that the best-known upper bound can be lowered.

For $k \ll \log \log N$, this is true [Gr24].

NOTE: [ESS89] derive a precise constant for which this is true, but $\ll$ would imply that it works
for any constant. We thus prefer a little-o statement.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ k N ∧ k N ≤ N) ∧ (fun N => ↑(k N)) =o[Filter.atTop] Green25.bestLower →

declarations.docstring:
Let $A_1, \dots, A_{100}$ be "cubes" in $\mathbb{F}^n_3$.
Is it true that $A_1 + \dots + A_{100} = \mathbb{F}^n_3$?

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $X, Y$ are two finitely-supported independent random variables taking integer values,
and such that $X + Y$ is uniformly distributed on its range. Are $X$ and $Y$ themselves uniformly
distributed on their ranges?
declarations.type_pretty:

  ∀ (X Y : PMF ℤ),
    X.support.Finite ∧ Y.support.Finite ∧ Green28.IsUniformOnSupport (Green28.indepSum X Y) →

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $A$ is a $K$-approximate group (not necessarily abelian). Is there $S \subset A$,
$|S| \gg K^{-O(1)} |A|$, with $S^8 \subset A^4$?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 29](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.29)
[Gr12] Green, Ben. "What is... an approximate group." Notices Amer. Math. Soc 59.5 (2012): 655-656.
[Br13] Breuillard, Emmanuel, Ben Green, and Terence Tao. "Small doubling in groups." Erdős Centennial. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2013. 129-151.
[Sa10] Sanders, Tom. "On a nonabelian Balog–Szemerédi-type lemma." Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 89.1 (2010): 127-132.
[CrSi10] Croot, Ernie, and Olof Sisask. "A probabilistic technique for finding almost-periods of convolutions." Geometric and functional analysis 20.6 (2010): 1367-1396.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ C c,
    0 < C ∧
      0 < c ∧
        ∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : DecidableEq G] (K : ℝ) (A : Finset G),
          1 ≤ K → IsApproximateSubgroup K ↑A → ∃ S ⊆ A, C * K ^ (-c) * ↑A.card ≤ ↑S.card ∧ S ^ 8 ⊆ A ^ 4

declarations.docstring: Such a conclusion is known with $|S| \gg_K |A|$ [Br13 Problem 6.5, CrSi10, Sa10].
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 29](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.29)
[Gr12] Green, Ben. "What is... an approximate group." Notices Amer. Math. Soc 59.5 (2012): 655-656.
[Br13] Breuillard, Emmanuel, Ben Green, and Terence Tao. "Small doubling in groups." Erdős Centennial. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2013. 129-151.
[Sa10] Sanders, Tom. "On a nonabelian Balog–Szemerédi-type lemma." Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 89.1 (2010): 127-132.
[CrSi10] Croot, Ernie, and Olof Sisask. "A probabilistic technique for finding almost-periods of convolutions." Geometric and functional analysis 20.6 (2010): 1367-1396.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (K : ℝ),
  1 ≤ K →
    ∃ c,
      0 < c ∧
        ∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : DecidableEq G] (A : Finset G),
          IsApproximateSubgroup K ↑A → ∃ S, c * ↑A.card ≤ ↑S.card ∧ S ^ 8 ⊆ A ^ 4

declarations.docstring: Suppose that $A \subset [0,1]$ is open and has measure greater than $\frac{1}{3}$. Is there a solution to $xy = z$ with $x, y, z \in A$?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 3](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.3 Problem 3)

declarations.docstring:
Do the following exist, for arbitrarily large $n$? An abelian group $H$ with $|H| = n^{2+o(1)}$,
together with subsets $A_1, ..., A_n, B_1, ..., B_n$ satisfying $|A_i||B_i| \ge n^{2-o(1)}$ and
$|A_i + B_i| = |A_i||B_i|$, such that the sets $A_i + B_i$ are disjoint from the sets $A_j + B_k$
($j \neq k$)?

NOTE: according to [CKS05, 4.1], the conditions should be $A_i + B_j$ disjoint from $A_j + B_k$ for
$i \neq k$. See `green_36.variants.cks05`.
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems #36](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.36)
[CKS05] Cohn, H., Kleinberg, R., Szegedy, B., and Umans, C. "Group-theoretic Algorithms for Matrix Multiplication" (Problem 4.7)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ ε > 0,
    ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ H x,
        ∃ (_ : Finite H),
          ∃ A B,
            ↑n ^ (2 - ε) ≤ ↑(Nat.card H) ∧
              ↑(Nat.card H) ≤ ↑n ^ (2 + ε) ∧
                (∀ (i : Fin n), ↑n ^ (2 - ε) ≤ ↑(A i).card * ↑(B i).card) ∧ Green36.Green36Property A B

declarations.docstring: Variant using the exact simultaneous double product property from [CKS05, 4.1].
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems #36](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.36)
[CKS05] Cohn, H., Kleinberg, R., Szegedy, B., and Umans, C. "Group-theoretic Algorithms for Matrix Multiplication" (Problem 4.7)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ ε > 0,
    ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ H x,
        ∃ (_ : Finite H),
          ∃ A B,
            ↑n ^ (2 - ε) ≤ ↑(Nat.card H) ∧
              ↑(Nat.card H) ≤ ↑n ^ (2 + ε) ∧
                (∀ (i : Fin n), ↑n ^ (2 - ε) ≤ ↑(A i).card * ↑(B i).card) ∧ Green36.SimultaneousDoubleProduct A B

declarations.docstring:
If $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is random, $|A| = \sqrt{p}$, can we almost surely cover
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $100\sqrt{p}$ translates of $A$? [Gr24]
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.39)
[BJR11] Bollobás, Béla, Svante Janson, and Oliver Riordan. "On covering by translates of a set." Random Structures & Algorithms 38.1‐2 (2011): 33-67.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun p =>
      have k := (↑p).sqrt;
      have c := 100 * k;
      ↑(Green39.proportionCoverable (↑p) k c))
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

declarations.docstring: "I do not know how to answer this even with 100 replaced by 1.01." [Gr24]"
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.39)
[BJR11] Bollobás, Béla, Svante Janson, and Oliver Riordan. "On covering by translates of a set." Random Structures & Algorithms 38.1‐2 (2011): 33-67.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun p =>
      have k := (↑p).sqrt;
      have c := ⌊1.01 * ↑k⌋₊;
      ↑(Green39.proportionCoverable (↑p) k c))
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

declarations.docstring:
Similar questions are interesting with $\sqrt{p}$ replaced by $p^\theta$ for any $\theta \le 1/2$. [Gr24]

NOTE: using $C p^\theta$ translates as stated makes the conjecture trivially false by the pigeonhole
principle. Indeed for a set of size $p^\theta$, we cover at most $C p^{2\theta}$ elements, which is
strictly less than $p$ for $\theta < 1/2$. We interpret the question as asking whether
$O(p^{1-\theta})$ translates suffice. This generalizes the main conjecture where
$\sqrt{p} = p^{1-1/2}$.
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.39)

declarations.docstring:
How many rotated (about the origin) copies of the 'pyjama set'
$\\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : \text{dist}(x, \mathbb{Z}) \leq \varepsilon\\}$ are needed to cover
$\mathbb{R}^2$?

In particular, can one find a better bound than the best-known bound from [KrLe25]?
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∃ ε₀ > 0,
    ∀ ε ∈ Set.Ioc 0 ε₀,
      have ans := sorry;
      ↑(Green41.minCopies ε) ≤ ans ∧ ans < Real.exp (Real.exp (Real.exp (ε ^ (-C))))

declarations.docstring:
Is there a better bound than the best-known bound from [KrLe25]?
This is an existential version of the main problem that does not require providing the bound explicitly.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ C > 0,
    ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Set.Ioc 0 ε₀, ∃ ans, ↑(Green41.minCopies ε) ≤ ans ∧ ans < Real.exp (Real.exp (Real.exp (ε ^ (-C))))

declarations.docstring:
[KrLe25] have established the first quantitative bound, showing via an analysis of [Ma15]'s method
that $\exp\exp\exp(\varepsilon^{-C})$ rotations suffice.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Set.Ioc 0 ε₀, ↑(Green41.minCopies ε) ≤ Real.exp (Real.exp (Real.exp (ε ^ (-C))))

declarations.docstring: Is $\varepsilon^{-C}$ rotations enough?
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ C, ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε ∈ Set.Ioc 0 ε₀, ↑(Green41.minCopies ε) ≤ ε ^ (-C)

declarations.docstring:
[Ma15] proved that for any $\varepsilon > 0$, finitely many rotations of the pyjama set of width
$\varepsilon$ cover the plane. This implies that the set we are taking the infimum over in `minCopies`
is non-empty.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → (Green41.coveringCopies ε).Nonempty

declarations.docstring:
Sieve $[N]$ by removing half the residue classes mod $p_i$, for primes
$2 \leqslant p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_{1000} < N^{9/10}$. Does the remaining set have size at most
$\frac{1}{10} N$?

We interpret "half the residue classes" as $\lfloor p_i / 2 \rfloor$.
references: [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.44)
[Er80] Erdős, Paul. "A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory." Annals of Discrete Mathematics 6 (1980): 89-115.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
    have remaining := {x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | ∀ (i : Fin 1000), ↑x ∉ A i};
    (∀ (i : Fin 1000), Nat.Prime (p i)) →
      StrictMono p → p 999 ^ 10 < N ^ 9 → (∀ (i : Fin 1000), (A i).card = p i / 2) → 10 * remaining.card ≤ N

declarations.docstring: The answer is affirmative if the primes are all less than $N^{1/2}$, by the large sieve. [Gr24]
references: [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.44)
[Er80] Erdős, Paul. "A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory." Annals of Discrete Mathematics 6 (1980): 89-115.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
  have remaining := {x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | ∀ (i : Fin 1000), ↑x ∉ A i};
  (∀ (i : Fin 1000), Nat.Prime (p i)) →
    StrictMono p → p 999 ^ 2 < N → (∀ (i : Fin 1000), (A i).card = p i / 2) → 10 * remaining.card ≤ N

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that a large sieve process leaves a set of quadratic size. Is that set quadratic?

The following very particular instance is probably the simplest [Gr24]:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ is a set with the property that
$|A \pmod p| \leqslant \frac{1}{2}(p + 1)$ for all sufficiently large $p$.
Is it true that either $|A \cap [X]| \ll X^{1/2} / \log^{100} X$, or $A$ is contained in the
image of $\mathbb{Z}$ under a quadratic map $\phi : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}$?
references: [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.47)
[GH14] Green, Ben, and Adam J. Harper. "Inverse questions for the large sieve." Geometric and Functional Analysis 24.4 (2014): 1167-1203.
[HV09] Helfgott, Harald Andrés, and Akshay Venkatesh. "How small must ill-distributed sets be." Analytic number theory 2 (2009): 224-234.
[Wa12] Walsh, Miguel N. "The inverse sieve problem in high dimensions." (2012): 2001-2022.
[Wa14] Walsh, Miguel N. "The algebraicity of ill-distributed sets." Geometric and Functional Analysis 24.3 (2014): 959-967.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    (∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Nat.Prime p → ((fun a => ↑a) '' A).ncard ≤ (p + 1) / 2) →
      ((fun X => ↑(A ∩ Set.Iic X).ncard) =O[Filter.atTop] fun X => √↑X / Real.log ↑X ^ 100) ∨
        ∃ P, P.degree = 2 ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, ∃ z, ↑a = Polynomial.eval (↑z) P
