[GrTa10] B. J. Green and T. C. Tao An equivalence between inverse sumset theorems and inverse conjectures for the U3 norm, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 149 (2010), no. 1, 1–19.
[Lo12] S. Lovett, Equivalence of polynomial conjectures in additive combinatorics, Combinatorica 32 (2012), no. 5, 607–618.
[LoRe17] S. Lovett and O. Regev, A counterexample to a strong variant of the Polynomial Freiman Ruzsa conjecture in Euclidean space, Discrete Anal.(2017), Paper No. 8, 6 pp.
[Ma19] F. R. W. M. Manners, Formulations of the PFR conjecture over Z, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 166 (2019), no. 2, 243–245.
[Sa12] T. Sanders, On the Bogolyubov-Ruzsa lemma, Anal. PDE 5 (2012), no. 3, 627–655.
[Ta08] T. C. Tao, A counterexample to a strong polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture, blog post November 2008, available at http://tinyurl.com/36j6hyxv.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ C > 0,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
      A.Nonempty → ∀ K ≥ 1, ↑(A + A).card ≤ K * ↑A.card → ∃ W T, Nat.card ↥W ≤ A.card ∧ ↑T.card ≤ K ^ C ∧ ↑A ⊆ ↑T + ↑W

declarations.docstring:
Which finite groups have the smallest biggest product-free sets?

We formalise this as: determine the supremum of exponents $\alpha$ such that every nontrivial
finite group of order $n$ contains a product-free set of size $\geq c n^{\alpha}$ for some
absolute constant $c > 0$. (The trivial group is excluded since its only product-free subset
is empty.) Kedlaya [Ke97] showed that $\alpha = 11/14$ is admissible, and Green suggests this
exponent may well be sharp; the candidate extremal family is the Ree groups ${}^2G_2(q)$,
$q = 3^{2m+1}$.
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.5)
[BaSo85] Babai L, Sós VT. Sidon sets in groups and induced subgraphs of Cayley graphs. European Journal of Combinatorics. 1985 Jun 1;6(2):101-14.
[Ke97] Kedlaya, K. S., *Large product-free subsets of finite groups*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 77 (1997), no. 2, 339–343.
[Ke09] Kedlaya, K. S., *Product-free subsets of groups, then and now*, Contemp. Math., 479, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2009, 169–177.
[Go08] Gowers, W. T., *Quasirandom groups*, Combin. Probab. Comput. 17 (2008), no. 3, 363–387.
declarations.type_pretty:
IsLUB
  {α |
    ∃ c > 0,
      ∀ (G : Type) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Fintype G],
        Nontrivial G → ∃ S, IsProductFree ↑S ∧ c * ↑(Fintype.card G) ^ α ≤ ↑S.card}
  sorry

declarations.docstring:
For the largest product-free subsets of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ of order $n$, the
best-known upper bound is $O(n^{8/9})$, due to Gowers [Go08].
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.5)
[BaSo85] Babai L, Sós VT. Sidon sets in groups and induced subgraphs of Cayley graphs. European Journal of Combinatorics. 1985 Jun 1;6(2):101-14.
[Ke97] Kedlaya, K. S., *Large product-free subsets of finite groups*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 77 (1997), no. 2, 339–343.
[Ke09] Kedlaya, K. S., *Product-free subsets of groups, then and now*, Contemp. Math., 479, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2009, 169–177.
[Go08] Gowers, W. T., *Quasirandom groups*, Combin. Probab. Comput. 17 (2008), no. 3, 363–387.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (S : Finset (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod p))),
    IsProductFree ↑S → ↑S.card ≤ C * ↑(Fintype.card (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod p))) ^ (8 / 9)

declarations.docstring:
Kedlaya [Ke97] observed, refining some work of Babai and Sós [BaSo85], that it follows from the
classification of finite simple groups that every finite group $G$ of order $n$ has a
product-free subset of size $\gg n^{11/14}$.
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.5)
[BaSo85] Babai L, Sós VT. Sidon sets in groups and induced subgraphs of Cayley graphs. European Journal of Combinatorics. 1985 Jun 1;6(2):101-14.
[Ke97] Kedlaya, K. S., *Large product-free subsets of finite groups*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 77 (1997), no. 2, 339–343.
[Ke09] Kedlaya, K. S., *Product-free subsets of groups, then and now*, Contemp. Math., 479, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2009, 169–177.
[Go08] Gowers, W. T., *Quasirandom groups*, Combin. Probab. Comput. 17 (2008), no. 3, 363–387.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ (G : Type) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : Fintype G],
    Nontrivial G → ∃ S, IsProductFree ↑S ∧ c * ↑(Fintype.card G) ^ (11 / 14) ≤ ↑S.card

declarations.docstring:
A good model problem would be to determine the largest product-free subsets of
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$.
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.5)
[BaSo85] Babai L, Sós VT. Sidon sets in groups and induced subgraphs of Cayley graphs. European Journal of Combinatorics. 1985 Jun 1;6(2):101-14.
[Ke97] Kedlaya, K. S., *Large product-free subsets of finite groups*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 77 (1997), no. 2, 339–343.
[Ke09] Kedlaya, K. S., *Product-free subsets of groups, then and now*, Contemp. Math., 479, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2009, 169–177.
[Go08] Gowers, W. T., *Quasirandom groups*, Combin. Probab. Comput. 17 (2008), no. 3, 363–387.

declarations.docstring:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a set of density $\alpha > 0$. Does $10A$ contain a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$?

More precisely: does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n \geq 1$ and all
nonempty $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with density $\alpha > 0$, the sumset $10A$ contains a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - C \log_2(1/\alpha)$?

The sumset $10A$ is defined as $\{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{10} : a_i \in A\}$, using the pointwise
scalar multiplication notation `10 • A` where `•` denotes the iterated addition of a set.

Note: We model $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ as `Fin n → ZMod 2`, which is an $n$-dimensional vector space
over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 50](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.6 Problem 50)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ C > 0,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
      A.Nonempty →
        have α := ↑A.dens;
        ∃ W v, v +ᵥ ↑W ⊆ ↑(10 • A) ∧ ↑n - C * Real.logb 2 (1 / α) ≤ ↑(Module.finrank (ZMod 2) ↥W)

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set of density $\alpha$. What is the largest size of coset
guaranteed to be contained in $2A$?

We phrase this by asking for the exact function $F(\alpha, n)$ giving the maximum dimension
of a guaranteed coset.
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.51)
[Gr13] B. J. Green, Restriction and Kakeya phenomena, notes from a 2003 course. Available at http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/rkp.pdf
[Sa11] Sanders, Tom. "Green's sumset problem at density one half." Acta Arithmetica 146.1 (2011): 91-101.
[Gr02] Green, Ben. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 12.3 (2002): 584-597.
[Ruz91] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Acta Arithmetica 60.2 (1991): 191-202.
declarations.type_pretty: sorry = Green51.guaranteedMaxCosetDim

declarations.docstring: It is known that $A + A$ must contain a coset of dimension $\gg_\alpha n$ [Gr13].
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.51)
[Gr13] B. J. Green, Restriction and Kakeya phenomena, notes from a 2003 course. Available at http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/rkp.pdf
[Sa11] Sanders, Tom. "Green's sumset problem at density one half." Acta Arithmetica 146.1 (2011): 91-101.
[Gr02] Green, Ben. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 12.3 (2002): 584-597.
[Ruz91] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Acta Arithmetica 60.2 (1991): 191-202.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (α : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, c * ↑n ≤ ↑(Green51.guaranteedMaxCosetDim n α)

declarations.docstring: It is known that $A + A$ must contain an arithmetic progression of length $\sim \exp(c (\log N)^{1/2})$ [Gr02].
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.51)
[Gr13] B. J. Green, Restriction and Kakeya phenomena, notes from a 2003 course. Available at http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/rkp.pdf
[Sa11] Sanders, Tom. "Green's sumset problem at density one half." Acta Arithmetica 146.1 (2011): 91-101.
[Gr02] Green, Ben. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 12.3 (2002): 584-597.
[Ruz91] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Acta Arithmetica 60.2 (1991): 191-202.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (α : ℝ),
  0 < α →
    α ≤ 1 →
      ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.exp (c * Real.log ↑N ^ (1 / 2)) ≤ ↑(Green51.guaranteedMaxAPLength N α)

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ has density $\alpha > 1/2 - C/\sqrt{n}$.
Does $A + A$ contain a subspace of co-dimension $O_C(1)$? [Sa11, Question 5.1]
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.51)
[Gr13] B. J. Green, Restriction and Kakeya phenomena, notes from a 2003 course. Available at http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/rkp.pdf
[Sa11] Sanders, Tom. "Green's sumset problem at density one half." Acta Arithmetica 146.1 (2011): 91-101.
[Gr02] Green, Ben. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 12.3 (2002): 584-597.
[Ruz91] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Acta Arithmetica 60.2 (1991): 191-202.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℝ),
    0 < k → ∃ c, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ α > 1 / 2 - k / √↑n, α ≤ 1 → n ≤ Green51.guaranteedMaxCosetDim n α + c

declarations.docstring: It is known that $A + A$ need not contain a coset of dimension $n - \sqrt{n}$ [Gr13].
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.51)
[Gr13] B. J. Green, Restriction and Kakeya phenomena, notes from a 2003 course. Available at http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/rkp.pdf
[Sa11] Sanders, Tom. "Green's sumset problem at density one half." Acta Arithmetica 146.1 (2011): 91-101.
[Gr02] Green, Ben. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 12.3 (2002): 584-597.
[Ruz91] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Acta Arithmetica 60.2 (1991): 191-202.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ α > 0, α ≤ 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Green51.guaranteedMaxCosetDim n α) < ↑n - √↑n

declarations.docstring: It is known that $A + A$ need not contain an arithmetic progression of length $\sim \exp(c (\log N)^{2/3})$ [Ruz91].
references: [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.51)
[Gr13] B. J. Green, Restriction and Kakeya phenomena, notes from a 2003 course. Available at http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/rkp.pdf
[Sa11] Sanders, Tom. "Green's sumset problem at density one half." Acta Arithmetica 146.1 (2011): 91-101.
[Gr02] Green, Ben. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Geometric & Functional Analysis GAFA 12.3 (2002): 584-597.
[Ruz91] Ruzsa, Imre Z. "Arithmetic progressions in sumsets." Acta Arithmetica 60.2 (1991): 191-202.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (α : ℝ),
  0 < α →
    α < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Green51.guaranteedMaxAPLength N α) ≤ Real.exp (c * Real.log ↑N ^ (2 / 3))

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set with an additive complement of size $K$.
Does $2A$ contain a coset of codimension $O_K(1)$?
references: [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.52)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ c,
    ∀ (n K : ℕ) (A : Set (𝔽₂ n)) (S : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
      S.card = K → A + ↑S = Set.univ → ∃ V, ↑V ⊆ A + A ∧ n ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) ↥V.direction + c K

declarations.docstring: Could $2A$ even contain a coset of codimension $O(\log K)$?
references: [Green's Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.52)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ C D,
    ∀ (n K : ℕ) (A : Set (𝔽₂ n)) (S : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
      0 < K →
        S.card = K →
          A + ↑S = Set.univ → ∃ V, ↑V ⊆ A + A ∧ ↑n ≤ ↑(Module.finrank (ZMod 2) ↥V.direction) + C * Real.log ↑K + D

declarations.docstring:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a balanced compact set (that is, $\lambda K \subseteq K$ whenever
$|\lambda| \leq 1$) and suppose that the normalised Gaussian measure $\gamma_n(K) \geq 0.99$.
Does $10K$ contain a compact convex set $C$ with $\gamma_n(C) \geq 0.01$?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 54](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.54)
Original formulation: M. Talagrand, *Are All Sets of Positive Measure Essentially Convex?*, in Operator Theory:
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (K : Set (ℕ → ℝ)),
    IsCompact K →
      Balanced ℝ K →
        0.99 ≤ Green54.gaussianMeasureInf K →
          ∃ C, IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ 10 • K ∧ 1e-2 ≤ Green54.gaussianMeasureInf C

declarations.docstring: The same statement is known to be false for 2K instead of 10K.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 54](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.54)
Original formulation: M. Talagrand, *Are All Sets of Positive Measure Essentially Convex?*, in Operator Theory:
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (K : Set (ℕ → ℝ)),
    IsCompact K →
      Balanced ℝ K →
        0.99 ≤ Green54.gaussianMeasureInf K →
          ∃ C, IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ 2 • K ∧ 1e-2 ≤ Green54.gaussianMeasureInf C

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that for every finite abelian group $G$ the spaces $\Phi(G)$ and $\Phi'(G)$,
obtained from kernels $\phi(g) = \mathbb{E}_{x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = g} f_1(x_2, x_3)
      f_2(x_1, x_3) f_3(x_1, x_2)$ with $\lVert f_i \rVert_\infty \le 1$
(where $f_i : G \times G \to \mathbb{C}$), still coincide when the
third kernel is required to depend only on $x_1 + x_2$?

Green guesses that the answer is probably 'no'.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 57](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
declarations.type_pretty: False ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [inst : AddCommGroup G] [inst_1 : Fintype G] [DecidableEq G], Green57.Φ G = Green57.Φ' G

declarations.docstring:
Do $\Phi(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})$ and $\Phi'(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})$ coincide?

Numerical evidence suggests the answer is **no**: the integer functional $a = (-1, -3, 3)$
separates the two spaces. A branch-and-bound verification over the phase variables shows
$\max_{\Phi'} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle < 6.112 < 6.115 \approx
\max_{\Phi} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle$.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 57](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
declarations.type_pretty: False ↔ Green57.Φ (ZMod 3) = Green57.Φ' (ZMod 3)

declarations.docstring:
For $G = \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ and the functional $a(0) = -1$, $a(1) = -3$, $a(2) = 3$,
does the support function of $\Phi$ at $a$ strictly exceed that of $\Phi'$?

Numerical evidence suggests the answer is **yes**:
$$\sup_{\varphi \in \Phi'(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle
  \;<\; \sup_{\varphi \in \Phi(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})} \operatorname{Re}\langle a, \varphi \rangle.$$

The DeepMind prover agent provided a formal proof, showing that $\frac{183095}{30000}$ separates the
support functions.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 57](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
declarations.type_pretty:
have a := ![-1, -3, 3];
True ↔ Green57.supportFn (ZMod 3) a (Green57.Φ' (ZMod 3)) < Green57.supportFn (ZMod 3) a (Green57.Φ (ZMod 3))

declarations.docstring:
Suppose $A, B ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ both have size at least $N^{0.49}$. Must the sumset $A + B$
contain a composite number?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 58](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 58)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∀ B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ↑N ^ 0.49 ≤ ↑A.card → ↑N ^ 0.49 ≤ ↑B.card → ∃ m ∈ A + B, m.Composite

declarations.docstring:
Is there an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, whenever $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is a set of squares
with $|A| ≥ 2$, the sumset $A + A$ satisfies $|A + A| ≥ |A|^{1 + c}$?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 60](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 60)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), (∀ a ∈ A, IsSquare a) → 2 ≤ A.card → ↑(A + A).card ≥ ↑A.card ^ (1 + c)

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $A + A$ contains the first $n$ squares. Is $|A| \geq n^{1 - o(1)}$?

It is known that necessarily $|A| \geq n^{2/3 - o(1)}$, whilst in the other direction there do
exist such $A$ with $|A| \ll_C n / \log^C n$ for any $C$.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 61](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 61)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ f,
    Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), Finset.image (fun x => x ^ 2) (Finset.Icc 1 n) ⊆ A + A → ↑n ^ (1 - f n) ≤ ↑A.card

declarations.docstring:
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 62](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.62)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    Nat.Prime p →
      have A := Finset.filter Nat.Prime (Finset.range p);
      ∀ (x : ℕ), 1 ≤ x ∧ x < p → ∃ a₁ ∈ A, ∃ a₂ ∈ A, ↑x = ↑a₁ * ↑a₂

declarations.docstring:
Is there always a sum of two squares between $X - \frac{1}{10}X^{1/4}$ and $X$?
We formalize this as an eventual statement for sufficiently large real $X$.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 66](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (X : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n, Green66.IsSumOfTwoSquares n ∧ ↑n ∈ Set.Icc (X - 1 / 10 * X ^ (1 / 4)) X

declarations.docstring: Green notes that a well-known, almost trivial argument gives an $O(X^{1/4})$ bound on the left.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 66](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C > 0, ∀ᶠ (X : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n, Green66.IsSumOfTwoSquares n ∧ ↑n ∈ Set.Icc (X - C * X ^ (1 / 4)) X

declarations.docstring: Does Ulam's sequence have positive density?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 7](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.1)
[erdosproblems.com/342](https://www.erdosproblems.com/342)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), Erdos342.IsUlamSequence a → (Set.range a).upperDensity > 0

declarations.docstring:
The **no-k-in-line problem**:
For $N \geq k$ and $k > 2$, the AllowedSetSize is $(k - 1) N$, i. e. on an $N \times N$ subset,
there is a set of $(k - 1) N$ points for which no $k$ lie on a line (and not such a set of bigger size).
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 72](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.72)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-three-in-line_problem)
[GK2025] Grebennikov, A. Kwan, M. No $(k + 1)$-in-line problem for large constant $k$. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17743
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {k N : ℕ}, 2 < k → k ≤ N → Green72.NoKInLineFor k N

declarations.docstring:
By the pigeon hole principle, the size of a subset of an $N \times N$ grid such that no $k$
points lie on a line is bounded by $\leq (k - 1) * N$ for $N \geq k$.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 72](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.72)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-three-in-line_problem)
[GK2025] Grebennikov, A. Kwan, M. No $(k + 1)$-in-line problem for large constant $k$. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17743
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {k N : ℕ}, k ≤ N → Green72.AllowedSetSize k N ≤ (k - 1) * N

declarations.docstring:
**Green's Open Problem 72 / No-three-in-line problem**:
The no-k-in-line conjecture holds for $k = 3$.
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 72](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.72)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-three-in-line_problem)
[GK2025] Grebennikov, A. Kwan, M. No $(k + 1)$-in-line problem for large constant $k$. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17743
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {N : ℕ}, 3 ≤ N → Green72.NoKInLineFor 3 N

declarations.docstring: Does the no-three-in-line problem hold when $N$ is big enough?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 72](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.72)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-three-in-line_problem)

declarations.docstring:
Given $n$ points in the unit disc, must there be a triangle of area at most $n^{-2+o(1)}$
determined by them?
references: [Ben Green's Open Problem 77](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.77)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ o, Filter.Tendsto o Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧ Erdos507.α =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ (-2 + o n)

declarations.docstring:
Suppose that $A$ is an open subset of $[0, 1]^2$ with measure $\alpha$. Are there four points in
$A$ determining an axis-parallel rectangle with area $\gt c \alpha^2$?
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∀ (A : Set (ℝ × ℝ)),
      IsOpen A →
        A ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Set.Icc 0 1 →
          A.Nonempty →
            have α := (MeasureTheory.volume A).toReal;
            ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂, {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧ c * α ^ 2 ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂|

declarations.docstring:
From [Gr24] "It is quite easy to show using Cauchy-Schwarz that there must be such a rectangle with
area $\gg \alpha^2 (\log 1/\alpha)^{-1}$."
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (α : ℝ) in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0),
    ∀ (A : Set (ℝ × ℝ)),
      IsOpen A →
        A ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Set.Icc 0 1 →
          A.Nonempty →
            α = (MeasureTheory.volume A).toReal →
              ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
                {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧ c * α ^ 2 * (Real.log (1 / α))⁻¹ ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂|

declarations.docstring: Let `A ⊂ R` be a set of positive measure. Does $A$ contain an affine copy of `{1, 1/2, 1/4, . . . }`?

declarations.docstring:
**Grimm's Conjecture**
If $n, n+1, \dots, n+k-1$ are all composite numbers, then there are $k$ distinct primes $p_i$
such that $p_i$ divides $n + i$ for all $0 \le i \le k-1$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimm%27s_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → 1 ≤ k → (∀ (i : Fin k), (n + ↑i).Composite) → ∃ ps, ∀ (i : Fin k), Nat.Prime (ps i) ∧ ps i ∣ n + ↑i

declarations.docstring:
**Grimm's Conjecture, weaker version**
If $n, n+1, \dots, n+k-1$ are all composite numbers, then their product
has at least $k$ distinct prime divisors.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimm%27s_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n k : ℕ),
  1 ≤ n → 1 ≤ k → (∀ (i : Fin k), (n + ↑i).Composite) → ∃ ps, ∀ (i : Fin k), Nat.Prime (ps i) ∧ ∃ j, ps i ∣ n + ↑j

declarations.docstring:
**Gromov's Polynomial Growth Theorem** : A finitely generated group has
polynomial growth if and only if it is virtually nilpotent.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gromov%27s_theorem_on_groups_of_polynomial_growth)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] [Group.FG G],
  GromovPolynomialGrowth.HasPolynomialGrowth G ↔ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G

declarations.docstring:
Infinite groups do not satisfy polynomial growth over `ℕ` for any degree `d` because when
`d = 0` this reduces to the unbounded nature of `growthFunction` while `n = 0` works when `d ≠ 0`.
Thus a finitely-generated infinite nilpotent group would be a counter-example to
Gromov's theorem when quantifying over all of `ℕ`, and so `n = 0` should be excluded.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gromov%27s_theorem_on_groups_of_polynomial_growth)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G] [Infinite G] {S : Set G},
  S.Finite → Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ → ∀ {C : ℝ} (d : ℕ), ∃ n, C * ↑n ^ d < ↑(GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction S n)

declarations.docstring:
Danilov proved that one cannot replace the exponent $1/2$ with larger number.
In other words, for any $\delta > 0$, there is no positive constant $C$ such that
$|y^2 - x^3| > C |x| ^ {1/2 + \delta}$ for all integers $x, y$ with $y^2 \ne x^3$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall%27s_conjecture)
L. Danilov, *The Diophantine equation $x^3 - y^2 = k$ and Hall's conjecture*, Mathematical notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR 32 (1982): 617-618
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ δ > 0, ¬Hall.HallConjectureExp (2⁻¹ + δ)

declarations.docstring:
Elkies' example $(x, y) = (5853886516781223, 447884928428402042307918)$ shows that such $C$ must be
less than $0.0215$. Note that simple `linarith` does not work here.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall%27s_conjecture)
L. Danilov, *The Diophantine equation $x^3 - y^2 = k$ and Hall's conjecture*, Mathematical notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR 32 (1982): 617-618
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (C : ℝ), Hall.HallIneq C 2⁻¹ → C < 215e-4

declarations.docstring: Original Hall's conjecture with exponent $1/2$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall%27s_conjecture)
L. Danilov, *The Diophantine equation $x^3 - y^2 = k$ and Hall's conjecture*, Mathematical notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR 32 (1982): 617-618
declarations.type_pretty: Hall.HallConjectureExp 2⁻¹

declarations.docstring: Weak form of Hall's conjecture: relax the exponent from $1/2$ to $1/2 - \varepsilon$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall%27s_conjecture)
L. Danilov, *The Diophantine equation $x^3 - y^2 = k$ and Hall's conjecture*, Mathematical notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR 32 (1982): 617-618
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, Hall.HallConjectureExp (2⁻¹ - ε)

declarations.docstring:
Let $P = (m_1, \dots, m_k)$ be a tuple of positive even integers. Let
$\pi_P(n)$ denote the number of primes $p\leq n$ such that $(p, p + m_1, \dots, p + m_k)$
forms an admissible prime constellation. Let $w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)$ denote the
number of distinct residues of $0, m_1, \dots, m_k$ modulo $q$, and let
$$
  C_P = 2 ^ k\prod_{\substack{q\ \text{prime} \\ q\geq 3}}
    \frac{1 - \frac{w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)}{q}}{\left(1 - \frac{1}{q}\right)^{k+1}}.
$$
Then
$$
  \pi_P(n)\sim C_P\int_2^n\frac{dt}{\log^{k+1}t}.
$$
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m

declarations.docstring:
Richards [Ri74] showed that only one of the two Hardy-Littlewood conjectures can be true.

[Ri74] Richards, Ian (1974). _On the Incompatibility of Two Conjectures Concerning Primes_. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 80: 419–438.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty:
(∀ {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m) →
  ¬∀ {x y : ℕ}, 2 ≤ x → 2 ≤ y → HardyLittlewood.SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y

declarations.docstring:
For integers $x, y \geq 2$,
$$
  \pi(x + y) \leq \pi(x) + \pi(y),
$$
where $\pi(z)$ denotes the prime-counting function, giving the number of primes up to
and including $z$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {x y : ℕ}, 2 ≤ x → 2 ≤ y → HardyLittlewood.SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y

references: [Har1974] R. Hartshorne, [Varieties of small codimension in projective space](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society-new-series/volume-80/issue-6/Varieties-of-small-codimension-in-projective-space/bams/1183535999.full).
[MO2010] [Evidences on Hartshorne's conjecture? References?](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/13990/evidences-on-hartshornes-conjecture-references)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme),
  CategoryTheory.Limits.HasFiniteCoproducts (HartshorneConjecture.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.VectorBundles S)

declarations.docstring:
There are no indecomposable vector bundles of rank 2 on $\mathbb{P}^n$ for $n \ge 7$.
This is Conjecture 6.3 in [Har1974].
references: [Har1974] R. Hartshorne, [Varieties of small codimension in projective space](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society-new-series/volume-80/issue-6/Varieties-of-small-codimension-in-projective-space/bams/1183535999.full).
[MO2010] [Evidences on Hartshorne's conjecture? References?](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/13990/evidences-on-hartshornes-conjecture-references)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  7 ≤ n →
    ∀
      (𝓕 :
        HartshorneConjecture.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.VectorBundles
          (ProjectiveSpace (Fin (n + 1)) (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec { carrier := ℂ, commRing := Complex.commRing }))),
      𝓕.rank = 2 → Nonempty (𝓕.Splitting (Fin 2))

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_seventeenth_problem)
Motzkin, "The arithmetic-geometric inequality". In Shisha, Oved (ed.). Inequalities. Academic Press. pp. 205–224.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (d : ℕ), Hilbert17.Hilbert17thProblemHomogenousPoly 0 d

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_seventeenth_problem)
Motzkin, "The arithmetic-geometric inequality". In Shisha, Oved (ed.). Inequalities. Academic Press. pp. 205–224.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Hilbert17.Hilbert17thProblemHomogenousPoly n 0

declarations.docstring: The Motzkin polynomial is non-negative everywhere.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_seventeenth_problem)
Motzkin, "The arithmetic-geometric inequality". In Shisha, Oved (ed.). Inequalities. Academic Press. pp. 205–224.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (x y : ℝ), 0 ≤ (MvPolynomial.eval ![x, y]) Hilbert17.f

declarations.docstring: The Motzkin polynomial cannot be written as a sum of squares of polynomials.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_seventeenth_problem)
Motzkin, "The arithmetic-geometric inequality". In Shisha, Oved (ed.). Inequalities. Academic Press. pp. 205–224.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∃ n, ∃ (_ : 0 < n), ∃ S, Hilbert17.f = ∑ i, S i ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
Hilbert's 17th problem: every non-negative multivariate polynomial is a sum of
squares of rational functions.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_seventeenth_problem)
Motzkin, "The arithmetic-geometric inequality". In Shisha, Oved (ed.). Inequalities. Academic Press. pp. 205–224.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {n : ℕ},
  0 < n →
    ∀ (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ),
      (∀ (x : Fin n → ℝ), 0 ≤ (MvPolynomial.eval x) f) →
        ∃ m g, (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ) (MvRatFunc (Fin n) ℝ)) f = ∑ i, g i ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
Hilbert's 17th problem for homogeneous polynomials: characterization of dimensions and degrees
where non-negative polynomials are sums of squares of polynomials.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_seventeenth_problem)
Motzkin, "The arithmetic-geometric inequality". In Shisha, Oved (ed.). Inequalities. Academic Press. pp. 205–224.

declarations.docstring: Every Lie group trivially admits a Lie group structure.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)

declarations.docstring:
**Hilbert's fifth problem** (Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin, 1952): every locally Euclidean
topological group is a Lie group.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
[Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)

[arXiv:math/0103145](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103145)

  [inst_3 : ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G], LieGroup (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) ⊤ G

declarations.docstring:
**Hilbert–Smith conjecture**: every locally compact topological group acting continuously
and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
[Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
[Pardon 2013, arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324)
[arXiv:math/0103145](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103145)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace G] {X : Type u_2} [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X]
  [ConnectedSpace X] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G] [inst_7 : MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X]
  [FaithfulSMul G X], Hilbert5.AdmitsLieGroupStructure G

declarations.docstring:

See [arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324).
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
[Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)

[arXiv:math/0103145](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103145)

  [ConnectedSpace X] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) X] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
  [inst_8 : MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X], Hilbert5.AdmitsLieGroupStructure G

declarations.docstring:
The conjecture holds when `G` acts by isometries on a Riemannian manifold, since `G`
embeds as a closed subgroup of the isometry group, which is a Lie group by Myers–Steenrod.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
[Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
[Pardon 2013, arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324)
[arXiv:math/0103145](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103145)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace G] {n : ℕ} {X : Type u_2} [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace X]
  [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X] [inst_5 : ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
  [LocallyCompactSpace G] [inst_8 : MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] [inst_11 : MetricSpace X]
  [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (↑⊤) X],
  (∀ (g : G), Isometry fun x => g • x) → Hilbert5.AdmitsLieGroupStructure G

faithfully on any connected finite-dimensional topological manifold. By the Gleason–Yamabe
theorem, this is equivalent to `hilbert_smith_conjecture`.

[Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
[Pardon 2013, arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324)
[arXiv:math/0103145](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103145)

∀ {X : Type u_2} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X] (p : ℕ) [inst_3 : Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
  [inst_4 : AddAction ℤ_[p] X] [ContinuousVAdd ℤ_[p] X] [FaithfulVAdd ℤ_[p] X], False

declarations.docstring: Every discrete space is homogeneous.
references: [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology." Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf

declarations.docstring: Every Metrizable space is ω-monolithic.
references: [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology." Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (X : Type u_1) [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace X],
  Homogeneous.CountablyMonolithicSpace X

declarations.docstring:
Problem 16 in [Ar2013]:
Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space not greater than 𝔠?
references: [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology." Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (X : Type) (x : TopologicalSpace X),
    T2Space X →
      CompactSpace X →
        Homogeneous.HomogeneousSpace X → Homogeneous.CountablyMonolithicSpace X → Cardinal.mk X ≤ Cardinal.continuum

declarations.docstring:
Problem 17 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every nonempty ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space contains a point with a
first countable neighborhood basis?

Note: `Nonempty X` is required since the conclusion asserts the existence of a point.
references: [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology." Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (X : Type) (x : TopologicalSpace X),
    T2Space X →
      CompactSpace X → Nonempty X → Homogeneous.CountablyMonolithicSpace X → ∃ x_1, (nhds x_1).IsCountablyGenerated

declarations.docstring:
Problem 15 in [Ar2013]:
Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space first countable?
references: [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology." Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (X : Type) (x : TopologicalSpace X),
    T2Space X →
      CompactSpace X →
        Homogeneous.HomogeneousSpace X → Homogeneous.CountablyMonolithicSpace X → FirstCountableTopology X

declarations.docstring:
Problem 13 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every infinite homogeneous compact hausdorff
space contains a non-trivial convergent sequence?
references: [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology." Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (X : Type) (x : TopologicalSpace X),
    ¬Finite X →
      T2Space X →
        CompactSpace X →
          Homogeneous.HomogeneousSpace X → ∃ s, Function.Injective s ∧ ∃ a, Filter.Tendsto s Filter.atTop (nhds a)

declarations.docstring:
Problem 14 in [Ar2013]:
Is it possible to represent an arbitrary compact hausdorff space as an image
of a homogeneous compact space under a continuous mapping?
references: [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology." Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (X : Type) (x : TopologicalSpace X),
    T2Space X →
      CompactSpace X →
        ∃ Y x_1, T2Space Y ∧ CompactSpace Y ∧ Homogeneous.HomogeneousSpace Y ∧ ∃ f, Continuous f ∧ Function.Surjective f

declarations.docstring: It is known that every Jordan curve admits at least one inscribed rectangle.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inscribed_square_problem)
[A Survey on the Square Peg Problem](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274622766_A_Survey_on_the_Square_Peg_Problem) by *Benjamin Matschke*
[arxiv/2005.09193](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.09193)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (γ : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
  Topology.IsEmbedding γ → ∃ t₁ t₂ t₃ t₄ r, InscribedSquare.IsRectangle (γ t₁) (γ t₂) (γ t₃) (γ t₄) r

declarations.docstring: It is known that every *smooth* Jordan curve admits inscribed rectangles of all aspect ratios.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inscribed_square_problem)
[A Survey on the Square Peg Problem](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274622766_A_Survey_on_the_Square_Peg_Problem) by *Benjamin Matschke*
[arxiv/2005.09193](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.09193)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (γ : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
  Topology.IsEmbedding γ →
    ContMDiff (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
        (↑⊤) γ →
      ∀ r > 0, ∃ t₁ t₂ t₃ t₄, InscribedSquare.IsRectangle (γ t₁) (γ t₂) (γ t₃) (γ t₄) r

declarations.docstring: It is also known that every $C^2$ Jordan curve admits an inscribed square.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inscribed_square_problem)
[A Survey on the Square Peg Problem](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274622766_A_Survey_on_the_Square_Peg_Problem) by *Benjamin Matschke*
[arxiv/2005.09193](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.09193)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (γ : Circle → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
  Topology.IsEmbedding γ →
    ContMDiff (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) 2
        γ →
      ∃ t₁ t₂ t₃ t₄, InscribedSquare.IsRectangle (γ t₁) (γ t₂) (γ t₃) (γ t₄) 1

declarations.docstring:
Show that every bounded linear operator `T : H → H` on a separable Hilbert space `H` of dimension
at least 2 has a non-trivial closed `T`-invariant subspace: a closed linear subspace `W` of `H`,
which is different from `H` and from `{0}`, such that `T ( W ) ⊂ W`. One needs the assumption that
the dimension of `H` is at least 2 because otherwise any subspace would be either `H` or `{0}`.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_subspace_problem),
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H]
  [CompleteSpace H],
  2 ≤ Module.rank ℂ H → ∀ (T : H →L[ℂ] H), Nonempty (InvariantSubspaceProblem.ClosedInvariantSubspace T)

declarations.docstring:
Every (bounded) linear operator `T : H → H` on a finite-dimensional linear space `H` of dimension
at least 2 has a non-trivial (closed) `T`-invariant subspace. This can be solved using the Jordan
normal form, which is
[not yet in mathlib](https://leanprover-community.github.io/undergrad_todo.html).
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_subspace_problem),
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : Module ℂ H],
  FiniteDimensional ℂ H →
    2 ≤ Module.rank ℂ H → ∀ (T : H →L[ℂ] H), Nonempty (InvariantSubspaceProblem.ClosedInvariantSubspace T)

declarations.docstring:
There exists a bounded linear operator `T` on the l1 space `(lp (fun (_ : ℕ) => ℂ) 1))` without
non-trivial closed `T`-invariant subspace [Read 1985](https://doi.org/10.1112/blms/17.4.305), see
also the first counterexample by Enflo [Enflo 1987](https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF02392260), submitted
in 1981.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_subspace_problem),
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ T, IsEmpty (InvariantSubspaceProblem.ClosedInvariantSubspace T)

declarations.docstring:
Every bounded linear operator `T : H → H` on a non-separable Hilbert space `H` has a
non-trivial closed `T`-invariant subspace. Such an invariant space is given by considering the
closure of the linear span of the orbit of any single non-zero vector.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_subspace_problem),
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H],
  ¬TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H → ∀ (T : H →L[ℂ] H), Nonempty (InvariantSubspaceProblem.ClosedInvariantSubspace T)

declarations.docstring:
Every normal linear operator `T : H → H` on a Hilbert space `H` of dimension at least 2 has a
non-trivial closed `T`-invariant subspace. If `T` is a multiple of the identity, one can take any
non-trivial subspace . If not, one can take any nontrivial spectral subspace of `T`.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_subspace_problem),
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H],
  2 ≤ Module.rank ℂ H →
    ∀ (T : H →L[ℂ] H) [IsStarNormal T], Nonempty (InvariantSubspaceProblem.ClosedInvariantSubspace T)

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_subspace_problem),
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {H : Type u_2} [inst : TopologicalSpace H], ¬TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H → Nontrivial H

declarations.docstring:
The **Jacobian Conjecture**: any regular function
(i.e. vector valued polynomial function from) `kⁿ → kᵐ`
whose Jacobian is a non-zero constant has an inverse that
is given by a regular function, where `k` is a field of characteristic `0`.

This is false: `F` has Jacobian determinant `1` but identifies
two distinct points, so it admits no inverse. This counterexample works in all characterstics.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {k : Type} [inst : CommRing k] [Nontrivial k],
  False ↔ ∀ {σ : Type} [inst_2 : Fintype σ] [inst_3 : DecidableEq σ], JacobianConjecture.JacobianConjectureProp k σ

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {k σ : Type} [inst : Fintype σ] [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] [inst_2 : Field k],
  JacobianConjecture.JacobianConjectureProp k σ →
    ∃ G,
      G.comp (JacobianConjecture.RegularFunction.id k σ) = JacobianConjecture.RegularFunction.id k σ ∧
        (JacobianConjecture.RegularFunction.id k σ).comp G = JacobianConjecture.RegularFunction.id k σ

declarations.docstring: Does the Jacobian conjecture hold in the two variable case?
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ {k : Type} [inst : Field k] [CharZero k], JacobianConjecture.JacobianConjectureProp k (Fin 2)

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {k σ : Type} [inst : Fintype σ] [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] [inst_2 : Field k]
  (F : JacobianConjecture.RegularFunction k σ σ), IsUnit F.Jacobian.det ↔ ∃ c, c ≠ 0 ∧ F.Jacobian.det = MvPolynomial.C c

The two-dimensional case, proved by Davies [Da71].

[Da71] Davies, R. O., _Some remarks on the Kakeya problem_. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 69 (1971), no. 3, 417–421.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakeya_set)
declarations.type_pretty: Kakeya.KakeyaSetConjectureDim 2

The three-dimensional case, proved by Wang, Zahl [WaZa25].

[WaZa25] Wang, H. and Zahl, J., _Volume estimates for unions of convex sets, and the Kakeya set conjecture in three dimensions_. arXiv preprint, arXiv:2502.17655, 2025.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakeya_set)
declarations.type_pretty: Kakeya.KakeyaSetConjectureDim 3

declarations.docstring:
The finite field Kakeya conjecture asserts that any Kakeya set in `𝔽_qⁿ` has size at
least `c_n · qⁿ` for some constant `c_n` depending only on `n`.
This was first proved by Dvir [Dv08]. The best known bound to date, due to Bukh and Chao [BuCh21],
establishes that any Kakeya set in `𝔽_qⁿ` has size at least `qⁿ / (2 - 1/q)^(n - 1)`.

[Dv08] Dvir, Z., _On the size of Kakeya sets in finite fields_. Journal of the American Mathematical Society 22 (2009), no. 4, 1093–1097.
[BuCh21] Bukh, B. and Chao, T.-W., _Sharp density bounds on the finite field Kakeya problem_. Discrete Analysis 26 (2021), 9 pp.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakeya_set)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {F : Type u_1} [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : Fintype F] {n : ℕ} (K : Finset (Fin n → F)),
  Kakeya.IsKakeyaFinite K → ↑(Fintype.card F) ^ n / (2 - 1 / ↑(Fintype.card F)) ^ (n - 1) ≤ ↑K.card

declarations.docstring: The Kakeya set conjecture: Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ have Hausdorff dimension $n$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakeya_set)
